Pour 2 cups plus 5 tablespoons water down the sides of the bowl (warm if cold day, cool if hot day).
Lightly flour hands. With dominant hand scooped, gently mix ingredients while rotating bowl with other hand, until dough has a stringy, soft string-cheese consistency.
Flour a work surface. Scrape dough out and knead 5-10 minutes, folding sides under and pressing into center, until dough comes together without flour pockets.
Transfer to a lightly floured large glass bowl. Cover and let rise in a warm, draft-free place until doubled, about 45 minutes (check at 30).

Flour a cloth-lined wicker proofing basket or cloth-lined colander. Turn dough out, shape into a taut ball: fold the top and bottom under to create a seam, then tuck the dough underneath itself diagonally to build surface tension.
Transfer dough seam-side up to the basket. Cover and proof until dough sits about 1/2 inch from the rim, about 2 hours.
Position rack in bottom third of oven; preheat to 475F/245C. Mid-way through second proof, place a lidded Dutch oven inside to heat.
Remove hot Dutch oven, lightly flour inside. Flip dough into it seam-side down. Score top with a sharp lame about 1/4 inch deep (hashtag pattern).
Cover and bake 20 minutes. Remove lid and bake until deep brown, about 35 minutes longer. Knock test the bottom for a clear sound.
Cool on a wire rack at least 1 hour. Store wrapped in cloth at room temperature up to 1 week, or freeze in bags up to 3 months.
recipes.notes: The signature 4-pound miche that built the Poilane empire. Apollonia recommends cutting into quarters for easier slicing.

recipes.name: Poilane-Style Rye Bread (Pain de Seigle)

ingredients.name: water, divided, plus more for rinsing
stone-ground 100 percent rye flour (medium), plus more for work surfaces

instructions: Activate the yeast in a small bowl with 1 tbsp lukewarm water; whisk and let sit 2 minutes until foamy.
Combine salt with 1 tbsp lukewarm water in another small bowl to partially dissolve.

Scrape sourdough starter into a large glass bowl. Add activated yeast to one side, sprinkle with rye flour. Add salt mixture to opposite side (do not let salt touch yeast). Add remaining rye flour and all bread flour on top.
Pour 1 cup plus 6 tbsp room-temperature water around sides of bowl to help dough detach. Mix until dough comes together.
Knead briefly on a rye-floured surface; rye dough is sticky and dense.
Place in a floured proofing basket; cover and proof until risen, about 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 475F/245C with a Dutch oven inside.
Flip into the Dutch oven, score top, cover and bake 20 minutes. Remove lid and bake until deep brown, about 35 minutes longer.
Cool on a wire rack at least 1 hour before slicing.
recipes.notes: Rye contains less gluten than wheat and absorbs up to 4x as much water, producing a dense, moist loaf with malty, chocolatey flavor.

recipes.name: Pain de Mie

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour, plus more for flouring work surface
unsalted butter, room temperature, divided into small chunks
neutral oil (sunflower or canola) for oiling pan

instructions: In the bowl of a stand mixer with the dough hook, combine bread flour, all-purpose flour, and sugar.
Warm the milk in a saucepan to 100-110F.
Activate yeast: whisk yeast with 1 tbsp lukewarm water; let sit 2 minutes.
Add activated yeast, salt, and pepper to flour mixture, keeping salt and yeast apart in the bowl.
Mix on low until incorporated, with black pepper flecks evenly distributed.
Add 2 tbsp lukewarm water and all the lukewarm milk. Mix low then medium until ingredients incorporate and dough pulls from the sides, about 1 minute.
Incorporate butter one tablespoon at a time, mixing until each addition disappears (about 1 minute each); avoid overworking.
Transfer to a buttered large glass bowl. Cover and let rise until doubled, about 2 to 2.5 hours.
Brush a 9x5 loaf pan with oil (Pullman pan for a flat top).
Flour work surface; flatten dough into an oblong, fold the short edges in, roll into a thick log the length of the pan. Place seam-side down in the pan.
Cover with lightly oiled parchment paper (or Pullman lid) plus a weight. Let rise until 1/2 inch below the rim, about 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 390F/200C. Place loaf pan horizontally on the lower-third rack.
Bake until risen and crusted, about 35 minutes. Remove lid (if using) and bake 10-15 minutes more until golden honey color. Up to 1 hour total if needed.
Unmold while warm; cool upside down on a wire rack at least 1 hour. Wrap in cloth in a paper bag, store at room temperature up to 5 days.
recipes.notes: France's answer to Wonder Bread - a fluffy, white sandwich loaf made with commercial yeast. A touch of black pepper adds gentle oomph.

recipes.name: Brioche

ingredients.name: unsalted butter (high fat content), room temperature, cut into bite-size pieces, plus more for greasing
all-purpose flour, plus more for work surfaces

instructions: Activate yeast in a small bowl with 2 tbsp lukewarm water; let sit 2 minutes until foamy.
Brush 2 large glass bowls generously with room-temperature butter.
In a stand mixer with paddle attachment, combine flour, sugar, salt, and activated yeast (keep yeast from touching salt).
Add 5 eggs and mix on low-medium until almost fully incorporated and dough comes together, 3-4 minutes.
Switch to dough hook. With mixer on low, add butter in 3-4 additions, letting each disappear before the next. Mix on low-medium until smooth, shiny, and pulling from sides, 10-12 minutes total.
Transfer to a floured surface, divide in half, shape into 2 balls. Place each in a prepared bowl, cover, and let rise until doubled, about 2 hours (max 2.5).
Grease two 9x5 loaf pans with room-temperature butter.
Shape each dough ball into an oblong the length of the pan; fold short edges in; roll into a log. Place seam-side down in pans.
Cover with cloth in a draft-free place; let rise until dough reaches top of pan, 1.5 to 2.5 hours.
Position rack in lower third; preheat oven to 350F/180C.
Beat the remaining egg for wash; lightly brush over loaves.
Use kitchen scissors to score the center of each loaf with short snips horizontally. Let rest uncovered 3-5 minutes.
Bake until light terra-cotta/gold, about 35-40 minutes. Do not open oven door during baking.
Cool in pan 2 minutes, unmold, and cool on a wire rack at least 1 hour. Store wrapped in cloth in a paper bag up to 5-7 days.
recipes.notes: Do not halve the recipe - the volume of two loaves is required. Extra dough can be refrigerated 2-3 days or frozen up to 3 months.

recipes.name: Savory Corn Flour Bread

ingredients.name: neutral oil (sunflower or canola) for greasing pan
corn flour (not cornmeal or cornstarch), such as Bob's Red Mill

instructions: One hour before baking, pound flax seeds in a mortar with a pestle until coarsely ground, about 2 minutes (or use a blender/coffee grinder).
Combine ground flax with 2/3 cup oat milk; let sit at room temperature at least 1 hour (up to 24 hours) until goopy like egg white.
Crush hazelnuts coarsely in a food processor or under a knife handle; avoid making nutmeal.
Brush a 9x5 metal loaf pan with oil.
In a large bowl, combine corn flour, flax mixture, yeast, hazelnuts, and remaining 1 cup oat milk.
Mix with a rubber spatula until thoroughly combined, with no corn flour pockets. Texture should be pourable like cake batter.
Pour dough into pan; note how far below the rim it sits.
Cover with a kitchen towel; let rise at room temperature (68-77F) until risen about 1/2 inch, around 2 hours. Avoid overproofing.
Position rack in lower third; preheat oven to 390F/200C.
Carefully transfer the loaf to the oven to avoid collapse. Bake until deep golden mustard color throughout and edges brown, 40-60 minutes (extra 10-15 if underdone).
Unmold and cool on a wire rack at least 1 hour. Store in cloth or paper bag at room temperature 2-3 days.
recipes.notes: Vegan and gluten-free. The flax-and-oat-milk mixture mimics an egg white's gluten-network function. Corn flour - much finer than cornmeal - is essential.

recipes.name: Savory Pain de Mie Pain Perdu

ingredients.name: sea salt, plus more to taste
2-inch-thick slices of 3- to 4-day-old Pain de Mie

instructions: Add medium tomatoes, curry powder, salt, and pepper to a food processor or blender; pulse until slightly chunky puree, about 1 minute.
In a large shallow bowl, whisk eggs until frothy. Whisk in tomato mixture. Add bread slices to soak.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
While pan heats, flip the bread so both sides absorb the liquid.
Combine cherry tomatoes, chives, the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper in a medium bowl; toss to coat.
When oil just begins to smoke, add bread; cook 1-2 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer to plates, top each slice with half the tomato topping, and serve immediately.
recipes.notes: Inspired by French pain perdu and Spanish pan con tomate. The pint of cherry tomatoes refers to 1 pint quartered lengthwise.

recipes.name: Sourdough Wheat Tartines

ingredients.name: 1/2-inch-thick slices Poilane-Style Wheat Loaf, preferably cut from the center

instructions: Turn the broiler on its lowest setting.
Arrange 2 slices of Brie on each slice of bread. Layer 3 slices of prosciutto on top of each, piling for texture. Sprinkle with freshly ground pepper.
Cut each tartine in half widthwise and place on an ungreased baking sheet (or leave whole for appetizer-style strips).
Broil until cheese melts and prosciutto crisps slightly, about 2-3 minutes. Eat immediately.
recipes.notes: A perennial bestseller at the Poilane cafe. Best with bread just past peak freshness - the cheese rehydrates the crumb. Variations: arugula, Brie, and fig preserves.

recipes.name: Sourdough Wheat and Rye Granola

ingredients.name: 2- to 3-day-old Poilane-Style Wheat Loaf, cut into 1-inch chunks, crusts removed
2- to 3-day-old Rye bread, cut into 1-inch chunks, crusts removed

instructions: Position a rack in the center of the oven; preheat to 325F/160C.
Add both bread chunks to a food processor; pulse to coarse breadcrumbs, about 2 minutes.
Add the nuts; process until roughly chopped, about 30 seconds.
Transfer to a large bowl, add puffed rice; combine with hands or spatula.
Add salt and honey; stir with a rubber spatula until evenly coated.
Spread in a deep ungreased baking dish no more than 2 fingers high (split between two dishes if needed).
Bake until puffed rice is golden, 35-40 minutes, crushing with a wooden spatula every 10-15 minutes to break up honey bonds.
Cool completely in the dish. Store in an airtight container at room temperature up to 3 months.
recipes.notes: Customize with different breads, nuts, and dried fruit. Designed to use up stale bread that's too big to discard but too dry to eat.

recipes.name: Oven-Baked Brioche Croutons
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350F/175C.
Cut each slice of Brioche into about 6 cubes (save crusts for breadcrumbs).
Arrange the cubes in a single layer on a baking sheet. Drizzle with olive oil; season with salt and pepper.
Bake until completely dry and light golden brown, about 10-15 minutes.
Cool completely. Store in an airtight container at room temperature up to 2 weeks.
recipes.notes: Use the crusts to make breadcrumbs.

recipes.name: Pan-Toasted Pain de Mie Croutons

ingredients.name: 1-inch-thick slices stale Pain de Mie, crusts removed

instructions: Cut each slice of Pain de Mie into about 6 cubes.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. In a small bowl, combine garlic and parsley.
Once oil is hot, add bread cubes in a single layer; stir to coat. Continue stirring until golden, 2-3 minutes.
Add about half the garlic-parsley mixture; stir to coat. Toast 1 more minute until parsley sticks and croutons are golden and dry.
Transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate; sprinkle with remaining garlic-parsley mixture. Cool before serving or storing.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature up to 2 weeks.

recipes.name: Caesar Salad with Flavored Brioche Croutons
instructions: Make the flavored croutons: in a food processor, combine anchovies, Dijon, lemon zest, and garlic. Process about 30 seconds until starting to come together.
Add 2 tbsp water; continue processing to a mostly smooth, pourable consistency, adding water 1 tbsp at a time if needed. Transfer to a small bowl.
Arrange the Brioche slices on a rimmed baking sheet. Brush both sides generously with the anchovy mixture.
Cover the tray with plastic wrap; refrigerate at least 6 hours and up to 24.
Turn the broiler on. Tear Brioche into 1-inch cubes onto the baking sheet. Drizzle with 3 tbsp olive oil and sprinkle with 3 tbsp Parmesan.
Broil, tossing once, until golden and dry, 2-3 minutes. Cool on the sheet.
Whisk the dressing: lemon juice, honey, 6 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Combine romaine, radishes, and 2 tbsp Parmesan in a large bowl. Toss with half the dressing. Add two-thirds of the croutons and remaining dressing; toss. Top with remaining croutons and serve.
recipes.notes: Anchovy flavor permeates the bread during the long chill, then the broil crisps everything quickly.

recipes.name: Breadcrumbs and Sourdough Wheat Pesto

ingredients.name: thick slice stale Poilane-Style Wheat Loaf, plus more to taste
parsley leaves, loosely packed, coarsely chopped with scissors
sea salt, plus more to taste

instructions: Slice the bread into a few larger pieces, then tear into smaller chunks by hand.
Place bread in a food processor; pulse to fine breadcrumbs.
Add walnuts, parsley, salt, and a pinch or two of pepper. Pulse until ingredients just come together, about 30 seconds.
Slowly add olive oil; continue pulsing until pesto forms a uniformly dark green, coarse paste. Taste and adjust seasoning. For a smoother pesto, add more olive oil and continue to pulse.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator up to 5 days.
recipes.notes: In Italy, breadcrumbs historically substituted for cheese in pesto. Brioche makes an airy crispy breadcrumb; sourdough is coarse and dense. Try mixing leftover bread types.

recipes.name: Rye Sable Cookies

ingredients.name: rye flour, plus more for dusting

instructions: In a large bowl, beat eggs and sugar with a handheld mixer on lowest speed until frothy, 1-2 minutes.
Add butter; beat on low until just incorporated, about 1 minute.
In a medium bowl, whisk rye flour and salt.
Add half the flour mixture to the egg mixture; bring together with a rubber spatula. Add the rest and bring together.
Mix with the handheld mixer on low until flour is fully incorporated and dough has the consistency of wet sand. Do not overmix.
Scrape half the dough onto a clean surface. Bring together into a disk about 1.5 inches thick, then shape edges into a square. Wrap tightly in plastic. Repeat with the other half.
Refrigerate both blocks 30 minutes.
On a floured surface, roll dough to about 1/4 inch thickness. Refrigerate the rolled dough 10-15 minutes if kitchen is warm.
Lightly flour a cookie cutter; line a baking sheet with parchment. Cut cookies close together to avoid re-rolling.
Transfer cookies to the parchment, cover with another sheet of parchment, and refrigerate 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350F. Bake uncovered until deep golden brown, 12-15 minutes (rotate halfway if baking two sheets).
Cool on the baking sheet until cool to touch. Store in an airtight container in a dry, cool place up to 3 months.
recipes.notes: Known in-house as 'punitions' (punishments) - Apollonia's great-grandmother told the grandchildren to come get their punitions and handed them cookies instead.

recipes.name: Ichiban Dashi (Kombu and Bonito Stock)
instructions: Cut the kombu so 30 grams fit in your pot — don't tear it, which can cloud the dashi.
Put the kombu in a heavy-bottom pot and pour in the cold water. Let it simmer at a low temperature (140F/60C) for about 1 hour without boiling.
Using tongs, remove the kombu from the pot. (Leftover kombu can be used for nibandashi.)
Bring the kombu broth to a light simmer. Add the katsuobushi and let simmer for 15 to 20 seconds — don't oversteep.
Lightly skim the stock with a spoon or ladle. Remove from heat.

Line a strainer with fine cheesecloth set over a bowl and gently pour in the dashi. Gather the edges of the cheesecloth, lift it out, and carefully squeeze any excess liquid over the bowl. Discard the katsuobushi.
Use the dashi immediately, or store covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
recipes.notes: Niki uses rishiri kombu for clarity and flavor. Look for the largest flakes (hanakatsuo) of shaved bonito. Makes about 60 oz.

recipes.name: Zukuri: Modern Rockfish Sashimi

ingredients.name: 2 pieces of rockfish from the upper loin
2 hearts of romaine, cut in half
Leaves of seasonal microgreens such as sorrel and shiso

instructions: Blanch the rockfish: prepare an ice bath. Bring a pot of water to a boil and remove from heat. Put the rockfish in a heatproof dish skin side up. Gently ladle hot water over the skin 1 or 2 times to curl the skin.
Transfer the fish immediately to the ice bath so it's still raw. After 15 to 20 seconds, move to a paper towel-lined plate and pat dry.

Cure the rockfish: mix the salt, parsley, dill, and grated lime peel in a bowl. Sprinkle a little cure on the bottom of a container, place the fish on top, then cover with the remaining cure. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 40 minutes.

Make the burnt romaine sauce: heat a pan over medium-high heat with 1 tbsp grapeseed oil. Add the romaine cut side down, sprinkle with salt, and cook until charred on each side, about 1 minute per side.
Blend the charred lettuce with the garlic and ponzu until completely pureed. Add grapeseed oil as needed to loosen. Taste and season.
Remove the cure from the fish, gently rinse under cold low-running water, and pat dry.
Cut one fish loin into thin slices (usuzukuri) using single strokes of the knife. Cut the other into slightly thicker slices (hiragiri).
Prepare garnishes: using a mandoline, cut radishes paper-thin and hold in an ice bath. Cut chives into 1-inch pieces on the bias. Cut thin half-moons from the lime. Perk microgreens in ice bath.

Plate: arrange overlapping radishes on one side, then place a few slices each of thick-cut and thin-cut fish next to them, folded upright. Intersperse chives and microgreens and add a slice of lime. Serve with the charred romaine sauce for dipping.
recipes.notes: Inspired by Adeline Grattard of Yam'Tcha in Paris — the parsley-dill cure is non-traditional but pairs the modern sashimi with a Japanese identity. The burnt romaine sauce also works as a marinade for chicken or fish.

recipes.name: Owan: Soup With Bone Broth

ingredients.name: Rockfish bones, leftover from preparing a whole fish
1/2 cup thick-sliced daikon, cut into half-moons, lightly blanched
1/4 cup 1-inch carrot pieces cut on the bias, lightly blanched
2 small shiitake mushroom caps, cut into quarters, blanched

instructions: Blanch the rockfish bones and collars: bring a small pot of water to a boil and remove from heat. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment, place the bones and collars on top, and ladle the hot water over them, draining off in the sink. Repeat, then flip and ladle again. Remove any scales from collars.

Place the blanched bones in a pot, breaking as needed to fit, along with the sliced onions. Pour in the dashi. Heat over low, bringing to a low simmer and skimming as needed. Simmer on low for about 40 minutes; the onions should be translucent.
Meanwhile, sake-steam the collars: place blanched collars in a steamer, pour 1/2 tsp sake over each, and steam for 4 minutes. Keep warm.
Using tongs, remove the rockfish bones from the pot and discard. Pour the broth through a cheesecloth-lined strainer into a large bowl.
Return the broth to the pot and bring back to a simmer. Season with a few pinches of salt and simmer for 2 more minutes.
Assemble bowls: place one piece of daikon, one piece of carrot, and one piece of shiitake side by side in each bowl. Top with a rockfish collar.
Carefully ladle the broth into the bowls, pouring to the side of the ingredients. Top with julienned ginger and scallions and serve immediately.
recipes.notes: The soup course is a light palate cleanser between the modern zukuri sashimi and traditional otsukuri sashimi, with a warm contrast. Use lidded soup bowls if possible — meant to be held one-handed and sipped slowly.

recipes.name: Otsukuri: Traditional Tuna Sashimi

ingredients.name: 1 cup julienned daikon from 1/2 medium daikon, peeled, trimmed, and rotary cut
1/4 cup scallions from 2 scallions, white and light green parts only
1 small Japanese cucumber, cut into 4 pine trees
2 pieces tuna loin, cut from akami
8 g wasabi paste grated from fresh wasabi root

instructions: Make the soy sauce: blend 9 parts soy sauce with 2 parts dashi, 1 part mirin, and 1 part sake (alcohol cooked off). Refrigerate until ready to serve.

Katsuramuki (rotary cut) the daikon: prepare an ice bath with a mesh strainer. Cut the peeled daikon into a 5-inch cylinder. Hold the blade lengthwise against the daikon at a slight angle and rotate the daikon against the blade, cutting a paper-thin sheet — keep both hands light and the knife moving gently. Continue until you reach the center.
Ken (julienne) the daikon: cut the long sheet into squares, stack, and julienne into 1/16-inch fine strips. Soak in the ice bath to crisp, then drain and dry.
Koguchigiri the scallions: thinly slice using the full blade pulled toward you. Rinse in ice water, drain, and dry.

Matsugiri (pine cut) the cucumber: cut off 1/3 of the cucumber and reserve. Halve the rest lengthwise. Lay flat side down and trim sides. Make lengthwise cuts partway through, then angle the knife about 45 degrees and cut partway through on a diagonal. Fan out to form a pine tree. Repeat to make 4.
For the toro: use a spoon to scrape the tuna meat from the trimmed sinew. Place in a bowl and mix gently with the scallions.
For the sashimi: square off two saku blocks from the tuna loin. Use hirazukuri to cut about 12 1/3-inch slices against the grain, with two-bite maximum size.

Create sashimi rosettes: slice the tuna very thinly at a 45-degree angle, cutting 20 slices. Arrange in 4 lines by slightly overlapping 5 slices vertically, then roll each line with chopsticks to form a rosette.

Plate: place a small mound of julienned daikon (tsuma) on each plate as a 'mountain.' Lean a shiso leaf against it, then arrange 3 slices of sashimi against the shiso at an 11 o'clock angle. Add a rosette next to the sashimi. Add the pine-cut cucumber to the center. Add a spoonful of the toro-scallion mixture next to the cucumber.
Garnish with white wasabi flowers or small edible blossoms. Form a small mound of grated wasabi at the side. Serve with a small bowl of soy sauce.
recipes.notes: Yama-tani-kawa ('mountain-valley-river') — the otsukuri plating should convey different heights and a sense of movement. Dab wasabi directly onto the sashimi rather than mixing it into the soy sauce.

recipes.name: Yakimono: Grilled Tuna

ingredients.name: 2 percent salt (by weight of the cucumber)
4 small tuna steaks, about 3 oz each, cut from the loin

instructions: Make the pickled cucumber: cut the Japanese cucumber into 1/4-inch discs. Weigh, then add 2% of the weight in salt and mix. Let sit 10 to 15 minutes and discard any liquid that leaches out.
Julienne 2 red shiso leaves and add to the bowl with the yuzu juice. Toss and chill until ready to serve.
Prepare the grill: ignite 8 to 10 pieces of binchotan in a charcoal chimney or directly over a flame. Heat until consistently glowing, 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Prepare the marinade: pour the sake and mirin into a shallow pan over medium-high heat and burn off the alcohol, 2 to 3 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine soy sauce, ginger, garlic, and sugar. Pour the heated sake-mirin mixture in and mix until the sugar dissolves. Add the tuna and marinate for 40 minutes.
Skewer the tuna using double skewers for each set, piercing against the grain to prevent breaking.
Transfer the binchotan to your konro or grill in a well-ventilated area. Divide the binchotan into 2 stacks of different heights for varied heat zones.
Place the skewers on the grill and move skewers or charcoal as needed. Grill until the marinade is caramelized and golden brown, about 4 minutes per side.
Place two overlapping shiso leaves in the center of each plate, top with two tuna steaks (overlapping), and add a mound of pickled cucumber alongside. Serve.
recipes.notes: Pairs well with sake. Binchotan charcoal produces vapors rather than smoke when fish fat drips on it, intensifying flavor. The pickled cucumber with yuzu balances the sweet-soy marinade.

recipes.name: Mushimono: Steamed Rockfish

ingredients.name: 1 russet potato, cut into large pieces and boiled
1 oz usukuchi soy sauce, light colored, not low sodium

instructions: Pre-steam the fish: place the rockfish fillets in a shallow bowl with a splash of sake and soy sauce and a pinch of salt. Place in a steamer over medium heat and steam for 4 minutes. Set aside.

Make the potato puree: put boiled russet potatoes and butter in a food processor. Add 4 oz dashi a little at a time while pulsing. Blend to a smooth puree (consistency like loose mashed potatoes). Season with salt.

Make the ankake: combine 8 oz of dashi with the mirin and usukuchi soy sauce in a saucepan over medium heat. In a small bowl, whisk the remaining 4 oz dashi with potato starch to make a slurry, then add it gradually to the saucepan, whisking constantly to prevent clumps. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Continue whisking while bringing to a boil to thicken. Once slightly thickened, keep warm. Leftover ankake keeps refrigerated for up to 5 days.

Place a couple spoonfuls of potato puree in the bottom of each of 4 small heatproof bowls. Divide the fish among the bowls, placing skin side up on top of the puree. Steam for 3 to 4 minutes (135F/57C to 145F/63C).
Garnish each bowl with the julienned lemon rind, ladle ankake over the fish in a thin layer, and garnish with the peppers and scallions. Cover with lids and serve immediately.
recipes.notes: Use the leftover rockfish fillets from the modern zukuri course in the spirit of mottainai. Ankake ratio is 12 parts dashi to 1 part mirin to 1 part usukuchi soy sauce. Reheat leftover ankake to use on steamed or sauteed vegetables with rice.

recipes.name: Agemono: Rockfish and Vegetable Tempura

ingredients.name: 3 qt rice bran or soybean oil, for frying
8 1/2-inch slices of rockfish (left over from cutting the belly loin)
4 pieces Japanese sweet potato, cut into 1/4-inch discs
Freshly grated ginger, squeezed of excess moisture, to taste

instructions: Fill a wide, deep pot or wok with oil to come at least 3 to 4 inches up the sides. Heat over medium-high to 350F/177C.

Make the tempura batter: set a large bowl over an ice bath and sift in the flour, baking soda, and potato starch. In a small bowl, mix the egg and 1 cup ice water. Add to the flour mixture and stir with chopsticks or a small whisk, leaving small lumps — under a minute. Keep batter on ice.
Prepare the rockfish and vegetables: put potato starch in an even layer at the bottom of a shallow baking dish.

Test the oil by dropping in a little batter — it should float and bubble. Lightly dust ingredients with potato starch, dip in batter to lightly coat, and fry in batches by ingredient until lightly golden, turning with a skimmer. Vegetables 1 to 2 minutes (shiso leaves 15 seconds), root vegetables 3 to 4 minutes, rockfish 1 to 2 minutes. Transfer to a rack or paper towel.
Make the tempura dipping sauce: mix dashi, mirin, and soy sauce in a 4:1:1 ratio in a saucepan over medium heat. Heat until it comes to a light simmer, about 5 minutes.

Place a small mound of freshly grated daikon in small bowls and top with grated ginger. Transfer dipping sauce to bowls. Serve the tempura on paper alongside small bowls of salt, lemon wedges, dipping sauce, and grated daikon.
recipes.notes: Don't overmix — chopsticks help you retain small lumps. Keep batter ice-cold. Don't fry more than half the surface area of the pot at once. Between batches, skim crumbs that would burn and darken the oil.

recipes.name: Agemono: Tuna Karaage

ingredients.name: 4 oz tuna marinade (from Yakimono: Grilled Tuna)
12 pieces sliced tuna (2.5 in long by 1 in wide and 1/2 in thick)
3 qt rice bran or soybean oil, for frying

instructions: Prepare the tuna: mix the tuna marinade with the dashi, sesame oil, and grated garlic in a bowl, and add the tuna. Marinate for 40 minutes.
Fry the tuna: fill a wide, deep pot or wok with oil to at least 3 to 4 inches up the sides. Heat to 350F/177C over medium-high heat.
Put potato starch in an even layer in a shallow baking dish. Toss the tuna in the potato starch and coat thoroughly. Sprinkle the panko over the tuna and toss again.
Fry the coated tuna in the pot a few pieces at a time without crowding, moving with tongs. Fry until medium golden brown, 1 to 2 minutes. Transfer to a rack or paper towel.
Prepare the sesame aioli: in a small bowl, whisk the mayonnaise, ponzu, and sesame oil until well combined. Transfer to small dipping bowls.
Place a mound of julienned cabbage in the center of each plate, top with overlapping karaage, and place a lemon wedge on the side. Serve immediately with the sesame aioli.
recipes.notes: Niki calls this 'tuna chicken' — karaage is traditionally fried chicken. Useful for tuna whose exterior has darkened from oxidation.

recipes.name: Shokuji: Quick-Pickled Vegetables

ingredients.name: 1/4 cup daikon (leftover core), cut into 1/2-inch-thick quarter-circles
1/4 cup sliced red bell peppers, seeds removed
1/4 cup julienned cooked kombu (leftover from dashi)

instructions: Prepare the brine: combine the water or dashi, rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small saucepan over medium-high heat. Bring to a light simmer and stir to dissolve the sugar and salt. Remove from heat.
Put the daikon, carrots, and peppers in a heatproof bowl and pour the brine over the vegetables. Let cool.
Serve immediately or store in a covered container in the refrigerator for up to 1 month.
recipes.notes: Uses a 2:2:1 brine — 2 parts water or dashi to 2 parts rice vinegar to 1 part sugar. Sometimes called mazu (sweet vinegar). Add aromatics or herbs such as shiso to change up the flavor. Itadakimasu!

recipes.name: Tortillas de Maíz / Corn Tortillas
instructions: Set up a hand grinder over a bowl. Add corn to the hopper with 1-2 tsp water and grind, adjusting water until the masa is finely ground, smooth, thick, and slightly sticky.

If using fresh masa, roll into 1-ounce balls and rest under a damp towel. If using masa harina, combine with about 1 cup water in a bowl, adding 1 tbsp at a time until the dough is smooth, thick, slightly sticky, and uniform. Roll into 1-ounce balls and cover with a damp towel.
Heat a nonstick griddle or clay comal over medium.

Line a tortilla press with nonstick plastic (not Saran wrap). Place a masa ball in the center, cover with a second sheet, and press firmly. Open, flip the masa, and press again. The tortilla should be about 1/8 inch (3mm) thick.

Peel the tortilla off the plastic and place on the hot griddle. Flip when the edges turn opaque (about 30 seconds). Flip again when it starts blistering (about 45 seconds). It should puff up in 10-15 seconds, then remove.
Repeat with remaining masa. Wrap finished tortillas in a clean towel inside a tortillero or covered container to keep warm.
recipes.notes: Store tightly sealed in the refrigerator up to 3 days, or freeze. Reheat from the fridge by sprinkling with a few drops of water before warming on the griddle.

recipes.name: Salsa Verde Cruda
instructions: Add all ingredients to a blender and blend on high until smooth.
Taste for seasoning and add more salt as needed. Serve immediately.
recipes.notes: Makes about 1,200g. Hearts of romaine can be substituted for the little gem lettuce. Choose a very ripe avocado.

recipes.name: Salsa Brava
instructions: Remove the outer skin from the onion. Cut in half and slice into thin half-moons. Separate the layers and place in a bowl.
Wearing plastic gloves, slice the habaneros perpendicularly into thin flower-shaped rounds (stems, seeds, and all). Add to the onions and mix with gloved hands.
Remove gloves. Add the salt, oregano, lime juice, and olive oil. Stir to combine.
Let the salsa sit at room temperature for about 20 minutes before serving.
recipes.notes: Makes about 1,100g. Pairs with seafood, tostadas, sopes. Use colored habaneros or onions for a more festive look. Stores in an airtight container in the fridge up to 2 weeks.

recipes.name: Tacos al Pastor / Achiote-Marinated Pork Tacos

ingredients.name: 1g chile de árbol, destemmed and seeded
18g sea salt, plus more for seasoning
910g to 1.4kg pork tenderloin, cut into bite-size pieces

instructions: Make the tortillas: Press and cook golf ball–size masa balls per the corn tortilla recipe.
Make the Adobo Rojo de Chiles: Turn on the exhaust fan. Heat a large nonstick pan or comal over medium-high. Toast the chiles, flipping once, until aromatic, 1–2 minutes.

Transfer chiles to a blender. Add tomatoes, onion, and garlic. Stir the orange juice into the achiote paste in a small bowl, then add to the blender along with the grapeseed oil, cumin, oregano, and salt. Blend on high until thick but smooth, about 1 minute.
Marinate the pork: Combine pork with 3 tablespoons of the adobo in a bowl. Cover and refrigerate at least 24 hours. Store remaining adobo in the fridge up to 3 weeks.

Cook the pineapple: Trim, peel, halve, and core the pineapple. Cut into bite-size chunks. Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat, add pineapple and a pinch of salt, and cook, stirring often, 15–20 minutes until softened, translucent, and butter is absorbed. Cool.

Cook the pork: Season pork with extra salt. Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high until shimmering. Add pork, reduce heat to medium, and cook, stirring often, until cooked through and most marinade has cooked off, 5–7 minutes.
Assemble: Reheat tortillas briefly on each side on a comal. Fill each with warm pork and 3 pieces of pineapple. Top with minced onion and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges and Salsa Verde Cruda.
recipes.notes: Plan ahead — pork needs at least 24 hours to marinate. The adobo sauce makes about 760g; extra keeps refrigerated up to 3 weeks and works on other meats, fish, or vegetables.

recipes.name: Salad Tacos (Cactus and Watercress Salad)

ingredients.name: 3g Maldon sea salt or another finishing salt
4 to 6 fresh corn tortillas, for serving

instructions: Combine cactus with sea salt in a large bowl. Rest 1 hour to draw out moisture.
Rinse cactus in a colander to remove sliminess. Cut paddles into 1/2-inch (12mm) strips.
Transfer cactus to a serving bowl. Add radishes, onion, watercress, and cilantro.
Whisk together oil, lime juice, and finishing salt. Dress the salad and toss to coat.
Spoon into tortillas and top with grated ricotta salata. Serve within 1 hour of dressing.
recipes.notes: If nopales are unavailable, summer squash works as a substitute.

recipes.name: Pescado a la Talla / Red and Green Roasted Fish

ingredients.name: 1 whole 1kg to 2kg whitefish, butterflied and deboned
240g dried black beans, soaked overnight and rinsed
1g chile de árbol, destemmed and seeded
18g sea salt, plus more for seasoning
80g Ocosingo cheese, queso fresco, or cotija cheese for serving

instructions: Soak the dried beans in cold water overnight. The next day, rinse and place in a pot covered by 10cm of water. Add garlic and epazote (or avocado leaves). Remove any beans that float.

Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover. After 30 minutes, stir, top with water if needed, replace lid. Continue simmering, checking every 10–15 minutes until beans are soft but whole. Season with salt and set aside.

Make the Adobo Rojo: Toast chiles dry over medium-high heat, flipping once, 1–2 minutes. Blend with tomatoes, onion, garlic, achiote-orange juice mixture, grapeseed oil, cumin, oregano, and salt until thick but smooth.
Make the Green Sauce: Combine garlic, parsley, oil, cumin, and salt in a blender. Blend 2–3 minutes until emulsified.

Prepare the fish: Preheat oven to 200°C (375°F). Grease a baking sheet with olive oil. Place butterflied fish skin-side down, salt, then spread Adobo Rojo across one side and Green Sauce on the other.
Roast 15–20 minutes until flesh is white and just visible beneath the sauces.

Make Frijoles Refritos: While fish cooks, heat oil or lard in a cast-iron skillet over medium. Cook onion until translucent, 2–3 minutes. Blend bean liquid with 240g cooked beans until smooth. Pour into skillet with onions, stir to combine; mixture should be silky and coat a spoon but still drip off. Season.
Serve fish on a platter with warm tortillas, refried beans topped with cheese, Salsa Verde Cruda, Salsa Tatemada, and fresh lime.
recipes.notes: Ask the fishmonger to butterfly the snapper-like whole fish. Rancho Gordo is a recommended source for dried heirloom beans. Ocosingo is a Chiapas cheese; queso fresco or cotija are easy substitutes.

recipes.name: Huevos Rancheros Divorciados

ingredients.name: 8 to 12 corn tortillas, leftover or already cooked
120g crumbled cheese such as cotija, panela, or queso fresco

instructions: Make the Salsa Roja Ranchera: Roughly chop onion, halve garlic and serranos. Place tomatoes, onion, garlic, serranos, and water in a covered dutch oven over medium-low heat. Cook 20–25 minutes until softened.
Cool 10 minutes. Transfer with juices to a blender, add epazote, and blend on high until smooth, 1–2 minutes. Season with salt.
Make the Salsa Verde Ranchera: Repeat the same process using tomatillos instead of tomatoes. After cooking and cooling, blend with cilantro and epazote until smooth. Season with salt.

Make the Huevos Rancheros: Heat grapeseed oil in a skillet over medium. Toast tortillas in batches, flipping once, about 1 minute total. Drain on paper towels. Spread refried beans across each tortilla.

Heat olive oil in a separate skillet over medium. Crack eggs into a bowl, then slide into the pan one at a time. Fry until whites are set but yolks are runny, basting whites with hot oil if needed, about 1 minute.

Assemble: Place one egg on each tortilla. Spoon salsa verde over the egg white on one tortilla (leaving yolk exposed), spoon salsa roja on the other. Salt, garnish with crumbled cheese, and serve immediately.
recipes.notes: "Divorciados" refers to the use of two distinct salsas, one red, one green. Tomatillos must be fresh; canned versions lack acidity. If tomatillos aren't available, double up on the salsa roja.

recipes.name: Salsa Tatemada / Charred Salsa

ingredients.name: 12g chile serrano, sliced in half lengthwise and deseeded

instructions: Heat a comal or cast iron skillet over high. Char the dried chiles and garlic 2–3 minutes until skins soften. Remove chiles to a bowl of warm water to rehydrate, at least 10–15 minutes.

Continue blistering garlic, then add the onion. After 3–4 minutes, remove the garlic to a molcajete or blender. Add fresh serrano cut-side down, whole tomatillos, and halved tomatoes flesh-side down. Flip serranos so both sides char.
Continue roasting 10–15 minutes, flipping occasionally, until everything is charred and cooked through.
If using a blender: combine all roasted ingredients, salt, and cilantro and pulse to desired consistency.

If using a molcajete: grind onion, one tomatillo, and garlic to a rough paste. Add remaining tomatillos and tomatoes plus salt and continue grinding until mostly smooth (pick out any large tomato skins). Add softened chiles and grind until incorporated. Stir in cilantro to finish.
recipes.notes: Makes about 760g. The molcajete yields a more rustic texture than a blender. Substitute jalapeño for serrano or dry chipotle for morita if needed. Keeps refrigerated up to 4 days.

recipes.name: Tostadas de Atún / Tuna Tostadas

ingredients.name: 20g chipotle in adobo, canned, seeds removed
140g leek, white part only, sliced into 3mm rounds
60ml freshly squeezed orange juice (from about 2 oranges)
480ml rice bran oil, safflower oil, or vegetable oil
340g sashimi-grade tuna, trout, or other fatty fish, thinly sliced against the grain
1 avocado, halved, pitted, peeled, sliced into 8

instructions: Make the Mayonesa Con Chipotle: Pulse egg, lime juice, salt, and chipotle in a food processor until combined. With motor running, slowly drizzle in the oil until the mayonnaise emulsifies and turns creamy, about 4–5 minutes. Scrape down sides partway through.
Prepare leeks: Soak sliced leeks in cold water, separate the rings, then dry completely on a clean towel.
Make the tuna marinade: Stir together orange juice and soy sauce. Taste; if not acidic enough, add lime juice. The mixture should be a touch sweet, salty, and acidic.

Fry the tortillas: Heat 480ml oil in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium-high to 180°C (350°F). Fry tortillas in batches, flipping occasionally, until golden and firm, about 1 minute. Drain on paper towels. Save the oil for the leeks.
Marinate the tuna: While tortillas cool, place fish in a bowl with the soy-orange marinade and set aside.

Fry the leeks: Reheat oil to 180°C. Add leeks, stir constantly so they don't stick, and remove with a slotted spoon as soon as they turn golden, 2–3 minutes. Drain on paper towels — they'll crisp as they cool.
Assemble: Spread a thin layer of chipotle mayo on each tostada. Distribute sliced tuna, top with fried leeks and a slice of avocado. Serve with lime wedges.
recipes.notes: Iconic Contramar dish since 1998. Use the freshest sustainable tuna or substitute farmed trout. Premade mayo can be stirred with puréed canned chipotles in a pinch.

recipes.name: Quesadillas Doradas / Golden Quesadillas (Huitlacoche)
instructions: Cut kernels off the corn cob if using fresh huitlacoche.

Heat grapeseed oil in a medium sauté pan over medium. Sweat onion until translucent, about 2 minutes. Add garlic and serrano, then huitlacoche. Reduce heat to medium-low, add more oil if needed, and cook 3–5 minutes until softened. Season with salt and stir in epazote. Cover and set aside.
Press golf ball–size masa balls in the tortilla press. Leaving the tortilla on the bottom plastic sheet, spoon 2 scant tablespoons of huitlacoche filling into the center. Do not overfill.
Seal: lift both sides of plastic and fold the tortilla, pinching the edges through the plastic and pushing out air. The shape should resemble an empanada.
Heat 960ml grapeseed oil in a Dutch oven to 180°C (350°F). Working in batches of 2–3, fry quesadillas, rotating, until all sides are golden brown, 8–10 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with Salsa Verde Cruda.
recipes.notes: Other fillings work well: ricotta, chicken tinga, braised greens, squash blossoms, or chorizo. Chanterelles or cremini can substitute for huitlacoche. Use fresh moist masa to avoid cracking.

recipes.name: Aguachile Con Camarón / Raw Shrimp in Lime and Chile

ingredients.name: 2 tsp sea salt, plus more as needed
240ml freshly squeezed lime juice (from about 8 limes), plus more
Maldon sea salt or another finishing salt

instructions: Remove shrimp heads and shells, reserving for stock. Devein the shrimp, butterfly, and clean. Set meat aside in a bowl.
Sprinkle shrimp with 1 teaspoon salt and stir. Cover with lime juice and let cure 4–5 minutes while you continue.

Make the shrimp stock: Rinse heads and shells. Simmer with 470ml water, the onion, celery, parsley, and bay leaf for 20–30 minutes, skimming. Strain. Reserve 60ml for the aguachile; refrigerate or freeze the rest.
Pickle onions: Place onions in a bowl with ½ teaspoon salt. Cover with lime juice; juice should turn pink.

Make the aguachile: In a blender combine 60ml shrimp stock, parsley, cilantro, half a serrano, remaining lime juice, and the juice the shrimp cured in. Taste, add 1–2 limes for acidity if needed. Blend smooth.

Assemble: Pour aguachile into a bowl. Arrange shrimp skin side down on a serving plate. Salt the shrimp lightly. Spoon aguachile over until covered. Top with cucumber, pickled onion slices, chiltepin or chile piquín, and finishing salt. Drizzle with olive oil just before serving with totopos.
recipes.notes: Don't make more than you'll serve — aguachile is best the day it's made. Source the freshest sustainable shrimp possible.

recipes.name: Tamales de Guayaba / Guava Tamales

ingredients.name: 20 corn husks, for wrapping the tamales

instructions: Soak corn husks in a large bowl of warm water while preparing the filling.

Combine piloncillo, cinnamon, and water in a small saucepot over medium heat. Halve guavas and scoop the flesh and seeds into the pot. Bring to a boil, reduce to low, and simmer 10–12 minutes until thickened. Meanwhile, slice guava peels into 1/4-inch strips.
Remove cinnamon stick. Blend filling smooth with an immersion blender, then strain into a clean bowl, pressing to remove seeds. Stir guava rind strips into the strained filling. Set aside.

Make the masa: Whip butter in a stand mixer on high until very fluffy, about 5 minutes. Add sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and star anise. With mixer on medium, add fresh masa in golf-ball-size chunks, one at a time, waiting for each to incorporate. Increase to high and whip 2–3 minutes until light as whipped cream.

Assemble: Pat corn husks dry. Spread 2 generous spoonfuls of masa into a husk with a well in the center. Add a spoonful of guava filling into the well. Seal by gently squeezing the masa around the filling, pushing out air, then folding the bottom of the husk underneath. Repeat.

Fill a deep stockpot with 2–3 inches of water and set a steamer basket inside (water shouldn't touch tamales). Stand tamales sealed-side down, packed snugly upright. Cover, bring to medium heat, and steam 1 hour, refilling water as needed. Tamales are done when firm to the touch.
Whip the heavy cream and sugar to soft peaks.
Serve tamales from the husk with whipped cream and extra guava filling.
recipes.notes: Whipping butter aerates the masa for a light texture. Corn husks suit firm fillings; banana leaves are better for soupy ones. If piloncillo is unavailable, substitute 220g brown sugar with 40g molasses. Other high-pectin fruits (plums, apples, pineapple, berries) work in place of guava. Freezes well; steam from frozen without defrosting.

recipes.name: Blackberry Atole
instructions: Make the fruit jam: Combine blackberries, sugar, and 200ml water in a small saucepan over medium. Cook, stirring, 5–6 minutes until berries break down. Blend smooth and set aside.
In a medium pot over medium heat, combine 1.5L water, piloncillo, and cinnamon. Simmer 2–3 minutes, stirring to dissolve the piloncillo. Remove the cinnamon stick.
Whisk in the fresh masa until smooth and lump-free.
Reduce heat to low and stir in the blackberry purée; cook 3–4 minutes until melded.
Pour into a blender and blend until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds. Serve hot.
recipes.notes: Try with raspberries in place of blackberries for a variation. Atole is a warm, traditional Mexican drink based on masa.

recipes.name: Kir Breton (Nonalcoholic Buckwheat Aperitif)
instructions: Two days before serving: Preheat oven to 250°F/120°C. Spread buckwheat groats on a baking sheet and toast 30 minutes until deep brown.
Cool the groats 10 minutes, then combine with apple juice in a large lidded container. Cover and refrigerate to steep 2 days.
Juice the lemon. In a medium saucepan over medium heat, combine lemon juice and black currant purée. Simmer until volume reduces by half, about 15 minutes.
Let the lemon–cassis mixture sit 5 minutes, then ladle through a cheesecloth-lined strainer into a container. Refrigerate until chilled, about 1 hour.
Strain the buckwheat-apple juice through cheesecloth into a container.
To serve, spoon 2 tablespoons of the lemon–cassis mixture into each champagne flute and top with buckwheat apple juice. Serve cold.
recipes.notes: A nonalcoholic adaptation of the classic Kir Breton aperitif.

recipes.name: Dehydrated Tomato Petals, Skins, and Powder (Tomato Enhanced)

ingredients.name: Flesh of 3 lb Early Girl tomatoes

instructions: Bring 4 quarts water to a boil. Preheat oven to 200°F/93°C.
Make an X-shaped incision on the bottom of each tomato. Blanch 15 seconds, then ice bath.
Peel tomatoes; quarter and carve away seeds.
Arrange skins and slices on parchment-lined sheets. Top with shallot, garlic, thyme, oil, salt.
Bake until skins are crisp and petals leathery dark red, about 1 hr 30 min.
Serve: lay petals on plate, grind skins to powder, sprinkle. Garnish with herbs and flowers.
recipes.notes: The skins ground to powder become umami tomato seasoning.

recipes.name: Tomato Confit (Tomato Illuminated)
instructions: Preheat oven to 250°F/120°C. Blanch and peel Sungolds.
Spread in roasting pan with garlic, shallot, basil, lemon peel, aromatics, salt.
Cover with grapeseed oil. Bake about 1 hour.
Make vinaigrette: whisk 2 tbsp confit oil with 1 tbsp sherry vinegar; season.
Serve drained tomatoes with petals, drizzle vinaigrette, garnish.
recipes.notes: Holds 4 days refrigerated.

recipes.name: La Tomate du Jardin: Tomato Salad with Crème Fraîche (Tomato Evolved)
instructions: Slice heirlooms; marinate with salt, lemon juice, sherry vinegar, olive oil.
Make tomato water from trim; simmer, strain through coffee filter.
Make tomato gel with agar-agar.
Season crème fraîche with lemon and fleur de sel.
Plate marinated tomatoes, vinaigrette, crème fraîche spiral, petals, confit tomatoes, gel, herbs.
recipes.notes: The flagship tomato course at Atelier Crenn.

recipes.name: Beet Tartare with Vadouvan Yogurt
instructions: Salt-crust roast beets at 375°F/190°C for 75 minutes; peel.
Mandoline-dice beets into brunoise; season.
Make vadouvan yogurt: simmer oil with spices, strain, mix with yogurt.
Make beet juice vinaigrette: juice 4 beets, reduce, season with vinegars and oils.
Mound, divot, fill with yogurt, decorate.
recipes.notes: Vegetarian riff on beef tartare.

recipes.name: Marinated Honeydew Ribbons (Melon Enhanced)
instructions: Carve honeydew; mandoline into ⅛-inch ribbons.
Marinate with lemon, lime, fleur de sel, oil 5-10 min.
Plate overlapping; finish with oil and salt.
recipes.notes: First of three melon recipes.

recipes.name: Grilled and Roasted Brilliant Melon (Melon Illuminated)
instructions: Preheat oven 375°F. Cut melon into wedges; marinate with aromatics and citrus.
Sear melon 5 min per side until caramelized.
Roast 7 min in marinade.
Cold-smoke with applewood 25 min.
Cube and serve with marinade, fleur de sel, micro cilantro.
recipes.notes: Brilliant (Canary) melon is the showcase variety.

recipes.name: Melon Salad (Melon Evolved)
instructions: Make melon balls from cantaloupe.
Make melon water; strain overnight.
Grill Brilliant melon, cube, marinate with aromatics.
Cold-smoke 25 min.
Make melon gel with agar.
Plate with honeydew ribbons, balls, gel, herbs.
recipes.notes: Combines three melon techniques.

recipes.name: Confit Leeks with Béarnaise Sauce
instructions: Preheat oven 325°F. Trim and clean leeks.
Warm oil with garlic, bay, thyme; add vinegar and water.
Confit leeks 30 min until tender.
Make béarnaise base: reduce wine, vermouth, vinegar, shallot, herbs.
Whisk over bain-marie with yolks and butter; season.
Plate leeks vertically, drizzle confit liquid, drape béarnaise, garnish.
recipes.notes: Bain-marie technique for the béarnaise.

recipes.name: Essence of Mushroom
instructions: Make mushroom stock: char onion, simmer with leek, thyme, garlic, cremini stems 1 hour.
Make gel with agar-agar; chill.
Confit egg yolks at 200°F, 20 min; cold-smoke with applewood.
Make foam: simmer stock and milk with lecithin; aerate.
Plate gel, yolk, sliced caps, foam, herbs.
recipes.notes: Cremini stems make stock; caps garnish.

recipes.name: Pommes Purée with Leeks and Beurre Blanc
instructions: Make leek fondue with butter and crème fraîche.
Fry leek matchsticks at 330°F 4 min.
Roast leek rounds at 350°F 30 min; grind to powder.
Make mashed potatoes in blender with butter and crème fraîche.
Make beurre blanc: reduce wine with aromatics, whisk in butter.
Plate fondue, dollops of potato, beurre blanc, fried leeks, powder dust.
recipes.notes: Highlights Brittany salted butter.

recipes.name: Grilled Asparagus with Crème Fraîche
instructions: Make court bouillon: simmer water with vegetables, herbs, lemon 25 min; strain.
Peel and trim asparagus; blanch in seasoned stock 30 sec to 2 min; ice bath.
Whisk crème fraîche with lemon, zest, fleur de sel, pepper.
Grill blanched spears 1 min per side; finish with lemon, oil, salt.
Shave raw asparagus into ribbons; ice bath to curl.
Plate crème fraîche bed, alternate grilled and blanched, curls on edge, garnish.
recipes.notes: Bonus court bouillon recipe included.

recipes.name: Vegetable Parmentier
instructions: Make vegetable stock; strain.
Boil potatoes; rice and combine with milk and butter.
Glaze diced carrots, onion, and zucchini separately, then combine with stock.
Layer in buttered dish: vegetables, mashed potatoes, comté.
Bake 375°F 20 min until bubbly.
recipes.notes: Vegetarian Hachis Parmentier.

recipes.name: Roasted Cabbage with Sauerkraut, Pickled Mustard Seeds, and Parsley Cream Sauce
instructions: Ferment sauerkraut 2 weeks with 2.5% salt.
Sear and roast cabbage wedges 325°F 20-30 min.
Make parsley oil; strain.
Pickle blanched mustard seeds in vinegar syrup.
Make crème fraîche sauce with cabbage juice and parsley oil.
Plate cabbage with sauerkraut, mustard seeds, sauce.
recipes.notes: Plan 2 weeks for sauerkraut.

recipes.name: Cheese Salad (Aerated Cheese Mousse with Lettuce Punches)
instructions: Simmer milk and cream; whisk in cheese, sugar, salt, pepper.
Blend smooth; chill 1-2 hr.
Whisk into mousse; pastry bag.
Cut lettuce into shapes with punch/cutter.
Make vinaigrette in spray bottle.
Pipe mousse spiral, spray lettuce, arrange with tweezers.
recipes.notes: Modernist French cheese course.

recipes.name: Fusilli With Basil-Mint Pesto and Toasted Bread Crumbs

ingredients.name: 8¾ ounces (250 grams) extra-virgin olive oil, plus more
3½ ounces (100 grams) freshly ground bread crumbs

instructions: Cook the pasta. Bring a large pot of water to a boil and season liberally with salt. Add the fusilli and cook, stirring occasionally, until al dente, about 8 minutes.

Make the pesto. Halve the garlic clove and rub its cut sides along the inside of your blender. Pour in the olive oil, then add the basil. Strip the mint leaves from the stem, add them to the blender, and add the stem to the boiling pasta water. Add thyme leaves to the blender and the branch to the water. Add half the Parmigiano and half the bread crumbs to the blender. With the blender on, slowly stream in ½ cup of ice-cold water until the sauce blends smoothly. Add the remaining Parmigiano, season with salt, and blend until smooth.

Toast the rest of the bread crumbs. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a small skillet over medium-high heat. Add the remaining bread crumbs and cook, tossing occasionally, until toasted and crunchy, about 4 minutes. Drain on paper towels.

Serve. Drain the pasta, reserving ½ cup cooking water. Return pasta to pot, stir in the pesto and more olive oil (about 30 g) to emulsify, adding cooking water by the spoonful for a silky sauce. Spoon into bowls and sprinkle with toasted bread crumbs.
recipes.notes: Substitute cavatappi or penne rigate if fusilli is unavailable. Mint and thyme replace traditional pine nuts, with bread crumbs adding body.

recipes.name: Tortellini in Rich Broth or Parmigiano Cream

ingredients.name: 1 pound and 5 ounces (600 grams) all-purpose flour, divided, plus more for rolling
3½ ounces (100 grams) beef shoulder, ground (you can substitute with veal)
1 whole chicken (3 to 4 pounds), preferably free-range and organic

instructions: Blacken the onions. Heat a small skillet over high heat; place onion halves cut-side down and cook, undisturbed, until blackened, about 15 minutes. Transfer to a large stockpot.

Prepare the chicken. Remove neck, place inside cavity. Place chicken in stockpot with onions. Add beef rib, carrots, celery, bay leaves, and Parmigiano rind. Crack half the peppercorns and add along with whole peppercorns. Cover with cold water.
Make the broth. Bring to a boil, reduce to gentle simmer, and cook until reduced by a third, up to 6 hours, skimming every 10-15 minutes. Strain through a chinois. Season lightly with salt.

Make the tortellini dough in two batches. Mound 250 g flour, well in center, add eggs and yolks. Fork the eggs then incorporate flour to form a dough. Add remaining 50 g flour and knead 10 minutes until smooth. Rest 30 minutes covered.

Make the tortellini filling. Cook beef and pork in a skillet until no longer pink, drain on paper towels, refrigerate to firm. Combine with mortadella and prosciutto and pass through a meat grinder. Stir in Parmigiano and nutmeg.
Form tortellini. Roll dough 1/16 inch thick, cut into 1½-inch squares. Place marble-sized filling on each, fold diagonally, seal, then wrap around fingertip to form tortellini.
Cook in broth. Bring broth to a boil, add tortellini and cook until they float. Spoon into bowls with broth.
Parmigiano Cream Variation: Simmer cream, add Parmigiano-Reggiano, stir until reduced. Toss cooked tortellini in the sauce.
Dairy-Sensitive Cream Sauce: Blend 200 g grated Parmigiano with 300 g boiling water; warm gently without boiling.
recipes.notes: You need a meat grinder. Broth can be made up to a month ahead and frozen. Two variations included: rich broth or Parmigiano cream.

recipes.name: Emilia Burger

ingredients.name: Lambrusco wine (or other acidic local wine)
10½ ounces (300 grams) freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, preferably aged 24 months
16 mini brioche buns, split in half
2 cups flat-leaf parsley leaves (for salsa verde)
1¾ ounces (50 grams) dried bread crumbs, preferably homemade
⅛ ounce (2 grams) olive oil–packed anchovies, drained
1¼ cups (300 milliliters) extra-virgin olive oil (for salsa verde)

instructions: Extract the gelatin. Pour wine 1 inch up the side of a steamer pot, place sausage in steamer tray. Cover and simmer 30 minutes over medium-low until fat/gelatin melt into wine. Strain into a tall container, chill at least 4 hours until layers separate. Reserve the gelatin middle layer.
Make the burger patties. Mix ground beef with gelatin, then with Parmigiano, until evenly combined. Rest covered in refrigerator at least 1 hour.

Cook the burgers. Form ¾-inch patties matching bun diameter. Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-high, lightly grease with olive oil. Sear both sides until well-browned, then stack and brown the edges. Rest 5 minutes.
Toast and build. Toast buns cut-side down. Bottom bun, dollop salsa verde, patty, dollop balsamic mayonnaise, top bun.
Balsamic Mayonnaise: Blend egg and balsamic on low until smooth. Slowly stream in grapeseed oil until emulsified and shiny. Season with salt.
Salsa Verde: Blend parsley, bread crumbs, capers, anchovies, white wine vinegar, olive oil, and 10 g ice water until smooth and thickened.
recipes.notes: Cotechino is steamed in Lambrusco to extract gelatin, which binds the patty. Sub local high-gelatin sausage and local acidic wine/beer/cider if needed.

recipes.name: Passatelli With Broth of Everything (Brodo di Tutto)

ingredients.name: 2¼ pounds (1 kilogram) finely ground bread crumbs

instructions: Prepare vegetables. Preheat oven to 150°F (65°C). Peel onions, reserving flesh; peel potatoes, reserving flesh. Place skins on a baking sheet with roughly chopped parsnips and celery root. Dehydrate at least 8 hours or overnight.

Make the broth. Increase oven to 350°F (180°C) and roast vegetables until caramelized, about 30 minutes. Transfer to a large saucepan with 1½ gallons (6 L) cold water and thyme. Bring to boil, reduce to bare simmer, cook 6 hours. Strain through chinois, season with salt.
Make the pasta. Mix bread crumbs, Parmigiano, mushroom powder, pinch salt. Add eggs and knead 3 minutes until smooth. Rest covered 15-20 minutes.
Cook the pasta. Return broth to simmer. Press dough through a potato ricer with the largest plate over the broth, cutting noodles 4 inches long. Cook until they float.
Serve. Lift noodles into bowls and ladle broth over.
recipes.notes: Use stale homemade bread for bread crumbs ideally. Vegetable scraps can be substituted seasonally — fava pods, spring onion scraps, herb stems for spring.

recipes.name: Beautiful, Psychedelic, Spin-Painted Beet

ingredients.name: 2½ cups (600 milliliters) apple cider vinegar, divided
1 ounce (30 grams) extra-virgin olive oil (red pepper sauce)
1 ounce (30 grams) smoked olive oil (yellow pepper sauce)
Rosemary blossoms or other small edible flowers
Pinch of finely ground dried rosemary
4 cups mixed green herbs (parsley with mint, basil, thyme)

instructions: Roast peppers. Heat oven to 350°F (180°C). Roast red and yellow peppers until skins blacken, about 40 minutes. Steam in a covered bowl, peel and seed.
Roast beets. Heat oven to 400°F (200°C). Wrap each beet in foil with salt and olive oil; roast 2 hours.

Pepper sauces. Chop red peppers, cook with half the vinegar and a pinch of sugar until vinegar evaporates. Blend with olive oil and cold water to syrupy consistency; strain. Repeat for yellow peppers with smoked olive oil.
Potato sauce. Boil potatoes, peel, pass through ricer, stir in warm milk, rosemary powder, garlic powder. Blend smooth with olive oil and water; season.
Herb sauce. Blanch herbs 5 seconds, shock in ice water, squeeze, blend with olive oil, salt, ice water until loose. Strain.

Plate. Cut beets into 1-inch disks, then cut a 3-inch round from the center. Brush with smoked olive oil and salt. Rewarm pepper and potato sauces. Splash all four sauces around plate, place beet in center, drizzle with balsamic, garnish with rosemary blossoms.
recipes.notes: Sauces can be made up to one day ahead. Inspired by Damien Hirst's spin paintings. Optional smoked olive oil, rosemary powder, garlic powder can be made or bought.

recipes.name: Sogliola al Cartoccio (Mediterranean-Style Sole)

ingredients.name: 1 whole fillet sole or other thin, firm-fleshed white fish
5 paper-thin slices of lemon, preferably organic
1¾ ounces (50 grams) Gaeta olives, or other small black Italian olives, pitted
1 whole egg, lightly beaten, for egg wash

instructions: Season and prepare the sole. Heat oven to 350°F (180°C). Cut fillet in half crosswise, salt the flesh side, stack smaller half on larger.
Build the packet. Line a baking sheet with parchment. Place fillet in center, top with lemon slices, tomato halves, olives, capers, parsley. Drizzle with olive oil.
Seal. Brush parchment edge with egg wash, top with another sheet, fold edges over and over to seal completely.
Bake 25-30 minutes until cooked through. Cut a slit to release steam, peel back paper, transfer fillet to plate and spoon aromatics over.
recipes.notes: Use Meyer or organic lemons; any small briny black olive works for Gaeta. Substitute turbot, sea bass, or snapper for sole.

recipes.name: Tagliatelle With Hand-Chopped Ragù (Meat Sauce)

ingredients.name: About 8 tablespoons (100 grams) extra-virgin olive oil, plus more
1 pound 2 ounces (500 grams) mild sweet Italian sausage
1 pound 2 ounces (500 grams) beef oxtails, bone in
17 ounces (500 milliliters) dry white wine, divided
8¾ ounces (250 grams) tomato concentrate (passata) or tomato paste
1 pound 5 ounces (600 grams) all-purpose flour, divided
1 small onion, cut into wedges (for tongue)

instructions: Cook the beef tongue. Simmer tongue in court bouillon (water, onion, celery, peppercorns, white wine, bay leaf) about 1 hour. Peel off membrane while hot, trim, cut into two 1-inch slices.
Make tagliatelle dough in two batches. Mound 250 g flour, well in center; add eggs and yolks. Incorporate flour gradually; add 50 g more and knead 10 minutes. Rest 30 minutes covered.
Form tagliatelle. Roll dough 1/16 inch thick, flour generously, roll like a cinnamon roll, cut crosswise into 3/8-inch ribbons. Unfurl and hang to dry 30 minutes.
Melt bone marrow. In a large Dutch oven over medium-low heat, melt marrow with olive oil. Add carrots, cook 5 minutes; add onions and celery, cook 5 more minutes.
Cook sausage. In a separate skillet over high heat, brown sausage with salt and pepper, breaking up. Blot fat with paper towel. Add sausage to pot.
Sear beef cheeks and oxtails. In same skillet, brown beef cheeks and oxtails. Deglaze with half the wine; transfer to pot. Sear tongue slices and deglaze with remaining wine; transfer.
Cook everything together. Tie rosemary and thyme with twine; add to pot with tomato concentrate, bay leaves, and chicken broth to cover. Cover with parchment round and simmer 2 hours until tender.
Purée sauce and chop meat. Pass sauce through food mill. Chill meat 30 minutes, then dice all meat into ¼-inch pieces (separate oxtail meat from bones). Stir meat back into sauce.
Cook the pasta in chicken broth until floating and al dente. Transfer to ragù, toss with Parmigiano and olive oil to emulsify, loosen with broth as needed.
Serve. Twirl pasta into nests and top with more ragù. Serve with crusty bread.
recipes.notes: Plan a full day. Hand-chopping (not pre-grinding) the meat lets it cling to the tagliatelle. Pasta and tongue can be prepared 2 days ahead.

recipes.name: "Better Than Panettone" Soufflé

ingredients.name: 1 cup flaky sea salt (for vanilla salt)

instructions: Dry panettone. Heat oven to 215°F (100°C). Tear panettone into bite-size pieces, spread on baking sheet, bake about 1 hour until brittle. Cool, then blend to fine crumbs. Stir in cornstarch. Increase oven to 350°F (180°C).
Whip yolks. In stand mixer with whisk, whip 7 egg yolks with 75 g sugar on medium-high until tripled in volume and ribbony.
Melt chocolate. Melt white chocolate with butter over low heat. Slowly pour into yolk mixture on low speed. Transfer to large bowl, stir in panettone crumbs.
Whip whites. Clean bowl. Whip 7 egg whites with a pinch of salt, slowly streaming in remaining 75 g sugar, until soft peaks.
Combine. Stir ⅓ whites vigorously into yolk mixture. Fold in half remaining whites until almost smooth, then fold in rest until smooth.
Bake. Divide among three 6-ounce ramekins on a baking sheet. Bake 9-10 minutes until puffed but soft in the middle.
Serve. Sprinkle with vanilla salt, top with candied orange peel strands and chopped hazelnuts.
Vanilla Salt: Scrape seeds from vanilla bean into bowl, rub into flaky salt until coated.

Candied Orange Peel: Peel wide zest strips from 2 oranges, slice into matchsticks. Simmer with 1 cup sugar and 1 cup water until sugar dissolves and mixture boils. Off heat, transfer to jar, refrigerate overnight.
recipes.notes: Works with any muffin-style quick bread (gingerbread, banana bread, carrot, chocolate muffins). Vanilla salt and candied orange peel are make-ahead garnishes.

recipes.name: Pumpkin Risotto

ingredients.name: 1 pound 2 ounces (500 grams) risotto rice, preferably Vialone Nano
4¼ cups (1 liter) freshly squeezed orange juice

instructions: Make pumpkin purée. Heat oven to 175°F (80°C). Halve and seed pumpkin (yield about 1 kg flesh). Peel and cube. Bake at least 8 hours or overnight until custardy. Blend with apple mostarda and amaretti until smooth.

Make risotto. Toast rice in olive oil over medium heat until fragrant. Reduce heat, splash of water to cool pan. Add orange juice 100 ml at a time, stirring until each is nearly absorbed before the next. Continue until al dente.
Finish. Stir in pumpkin purée. Off heat, drizzle olive oil and a splash of water for a smooth sauce.
Plate. Spoon onto warm plate in thin layer. Garnish with almonds, amaretti crumbs, and apple mostarda.
recipes.notes: Substitute any winter squash. A chocolate-orange variation drizzles dark chocolate, candied orange purée, and a blackened orange garnish over the risotto.

recipes.name: Smoky Marinated Feta

ingredients.name: 2 blocks Greek feta (360 g), cut into ½-inch cubes

instructions: Heat a small sauté pan over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the garlic and cook 3-4 minutes, turning halfway, until cloves are charred.
Add lemon strips and bay leaves; cook about 90 seconds until lightly charred.
Add chipotle chili flakes and stir 30 seconds until toasted and fragrant. Remove from heat, then add oil, salt, and paprika. Stir 30 seconds to combine.
Add feta to oil; stir gently so each cube is coated. Transfer to a shallow container. Marinate at room temp if eating soon, or refrigerate up to 5 days.
recipes.notes: Keeps up to 5 days refrigerated; flavors deepen over time. Used in Pea Spread With Smoky Marinated Feta.

recipes.name: Tahini Sauce

ingredients.name: A pinch of salt, or to taste
3 tbsp water, plus 1 tsp water, or as needed

instructions: Combine all ingredients except water in a bowl and whisk to combine.
Slowly add water while whisking until mixture is smooth and pourable. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Use immediately at room temperature or refrigerate in a sealed container up to 5 days.
recipes.notes: Drizzle over kebabs, chopped salads, or roasted vegetables.

recipes.name: Confit Garlic Oil
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Cover and cook until garlic is soft and just beginning to color, 20-25 minutes.
Leave the lid on, remove from heat, and set aside for 10 minutes so garlic finishes cooking in the residual heat of the oil.
Strain oil into a clean glass jar and spoon in garlic, thyme, and chili. Once cool, transfer to a sterilized airtight jar and store at room temp for several weeks.
recipes.notes: Drizzle over salads or dip with bread. Used in Hummus With Confit Garlic and Tahini.

recipes.name: Labneh
instructions: Add yogurt and salt to a medium bowl and mix well.
Line a colander with muslin or cheesecloth large enough to hang over the sides; place colander over a bowl.
Transfer yogurt to the center of the cheesecloth and fold the overhang so yogurt is completely covered.
Weight down with cans/jars and refrigerate. Drain at least 12 and up to 48 hours.
Discard collected water. Labneh keeps in an airtight jar in the refrigerator up to 5 days, sealed with a thin layer of olive oil on top.
recipes.notes: Avoid set Greek yogurt — it won't drain properly. Sheep's milk yields tangier labneh; cow's milk creamier.

recipes.name: Quick-Pickled Chilies

ingredients.name: 2 small mild red chilies, thinly sliced, seeds and all

instructions: Add vinegar, sugar, and salt to a small bowl, stirring to dissolve the sugar.
Add chilies, stir well to combine, and leave to pickle at least 30 minutes before using.
If not using immediately, store in the refrigerator in an airtight container.
recipes.notes: Try them on grilled vegetables or roasted chicken. Used in Roasted Eggplant Salad.

recipes.name: Quick Lemon Paste

ingredients.name: 1 large lemon, end trimmed, sliced into ¼-inch-thin rounds, seeds removed

instructions: Combine all ingredients in a small saucepan over medium-high heat. Simmer until salt dissolves, 1-2 minutes.
Lower heat to medium-low, cover, and cook until lemon rinds look translucent, about 12 minutes.
Cool slightly, then transfer to a food processor and blitz until smooth and thick. Add a tablespoon of water if needed.
Transfer to an airtight container, pour a thin layer of olive oil over the top, cover, and refrigerate up to 2 weeks.
recipes.notes: A speed-up of traditional preserved lemons (which take 2-3 weeks).

recipes.name: Saffron Water
instructions: Soak saffron threads in hot water for at least 30 minutes (or overnight). Color intensifies as the saffron soaks.
Store in a sealed jar at room temperature for several weeks.
recipes.notes: A little goes a long way — use in risotto, crepe batter, or rice pudding.

recipes.name: Za'atar Oil
instructions: Combine za'atar and olive oil in a small serving bowl.
If not using immediately, store in an airtight container at room temperature for several weeks. Stir before using.
recipes.notes: Spread over pizza dough instead of tomato sauce, or spoon over roasted chicken, hummus, or butter bean mash.

recipes.name: Dukkah

ingredients.name: 1½ tbsp black and white sesame seeds

instructions: In a small saucepan over medium heat, toast coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and sesame seeds, shaking the pan occasionally, until fragrant, 2-3 minutes.
Add toasted spices and all remaining ingredients to a food processor and pulse a few times until nuts and seeds are roughly chopped.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for several weeks.
recipes.notes: Egyptian condiment — sprinkle over fish, eggs, or roasted carrots. Variations: pistachios, walnuts, mint, za'atar.

recipes.name: Sumac-Pickled Onions

ingredients.name: 1 medium red onion, thinly sliced into half-moons

instructions: Add all ingredients to a small bowl and toss well to combine.
Allow to soften and pickle at least 20 minutes before serving, or refrigerate in a sealed airtight container up to 3 days.
recipes.notes: Pairs especially well on roasted chicken, kebabs, or rice dishes. Used in Smacked Cucumber Salad.

recipes.name: Quick Shatta

ingredients.name: 90 g mild red chilies, such as Fresno chilies (about 6), roughly chopped

instructions: Add chilies, tomatoes, and salt to a food processor and pulse a few times until coarsely chopped but not puréed.
Add vinegar and olive oil, and pulse 1-2 times more until just incorporated.
Transfer to a small bowl. If not using immediately, transfer to an airtight container and pour enough olive oil over to seal the top. Refrigerate up to 1 week.
recipes.notes: Yotam's quick version uses cider vinegar instead of fermenting. Spoon over sandwiches, hummus, kebabs.

recipes.name: Rose Harissa

ingredients.name: 40 g dried Kashmiri red chilies or guajillo chilies
1½ tsp Kashmiri chili powder, or paprika

instructions: Place a large frying pan over high heat. Once hot, add dried chilies and garlic. Toast until fragrant and charred, about 2 minutes. Pick out garlic and set aside. Transfer chilies to a heat-proof bowl.
Pour boiling water over the chilies to cover, weigh down with a small plate, and soak 30 minutes. Drain and roughly chop, then add to a food processor.

Add cumin, coriander, and caraway seeds to the same pan and toast over medium-high heat until fragrant, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a mortar and pestle and roughly crush, then add to the food processor along with garlic, tomato paste, rose petals, sugar, and chili powder. Pulse until roughly combined.
Add lemon juice, half the rosewater, vinegar, 4 tbsp olive oil, and a pinch of salt. Blitz to a coarse paste.
Transfer to a bowl and gently stir in remaining rosewater and remaining 4 tbsp olive oil.
Transfer to a sterilized airtight jar and refrigerate, covered with a layer of oil, for several weeks.
recipes.notes: Remove stems and seeds after rehydrating to reduce heat. Used in Green Herb Shakshuka and Roasted Cauliflower.

recipes.name: Muhammara

ingredients.name: 5 red bell peppers, cored, seeded, and quartered
1 white onion, peeled and roughly chopped
2 plum or Roma tomatoes, halved lengthwise, stems removed
100 g walnuts, toasted and roughly chopped
100 g pomegranate seeds, plus 1 tbsp for serving
1 tbsp parsley leaves, roughly chopped, for serving

instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C/425°F.
Add peppers, onion, tomatoes, and chili to a large parchment-lined baking tray. Toss with 3 tbsp oil, ½ tsp salt, and plenty of black pepper. Roast 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, add tomato paste and 1 tbsp oil to a small frying pan over medium heat; cook 5-7 minutes, stirring, until tomato paste is deep red and caramelized. Set aside.
Add cumin and coriander seeds to a small pan and toast over medium heat until aromatic and popping, 1-2 minutes. Grind into a coarse powder with a mortar and pestle.
Remove vegetables from oven, add garlic, mix lightly, return to oven and roast another 20 minutes or until softened and lightly charred.

Once cool enough to handle, peel and discard tomato and pepper skins. Add roasted vegetables, tomato paste mixture, ground spices, 1 tbsp pomegranate molasses, ½ tsp salt, and pepper to food processor. Pulse to a coarse paste, slightly chunky. Add walnuts and pulse briefly. Stir in pomegranate seeds.
Transfer to a serving bowl with a slight well in the center. Garnish with extra pomegranate seeds and parsley, then drizzle with remaining tbsp each pomegranate molasses and olive oil.
recipes.notes: Syrian/Lebanese roasted pepper dip. Serve with warm flatbread.

recipes.name: Pea Spread With Smoky Marinated Feta

ingredients.name: 100 g Smoky Marinated Feta, plus 3-4 tbsp oil from marinade
1 lemon; 1½ tsp finely grated zest, 2 tbsp juice
½ tsp cumin seeds, toasted and roughly crushed

instructions: Make the Smoky Marinated Feta (see separate recipe).
Add peas, tarragon, mint, garlic, lemon zest and juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper to a food processor. Pulse to a coarse paste. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Spread pea mixture onto a plate and top with Smoky Marinated Feta, adding some garlic cloves and lemon strips from the marinade.
Spoon a generous amount of aromatic smoky feta oil (about 3-4 tbsp) over the spread. Sprinkle with cumin.
recipes.notes: Serve with warm flatbreads or crudités. A dark plate maximizes visual contrast.

recipes.name: Hummus With Confit Garlic and Tahini

ingredients.name: 12 confit garlic cloves, plus 4 tbsp Confit Garlic Oil
550 g cooked chickpeas (see Basic Chickpeas, or canned)
5 tbsp plus 2 tsp ice-cold water, plus extra

instructions: Make the Tahini Sauce and Confit Garlic Oil (see separate recipes).
Set 100 g cooked chickpeas aside in a small bowl.

Add remaining chickpeas, tahini paste, 8 confit garlic cloves, ½ tsp salt, and lemon juice to a food processor. Blitz until smooth, 2-3 minutes. With machine running, slowly drizzle in ice water until completely smooth and aerated. Adjust seasoning.
Add parsley, 2 tbsp Confit Garlic Oil, and a pinch of salt to bowl with reserved chickpeas; stir.

Transfer hummus to a shallow platter and smooth with the back of a spoon, creating a slight well. Spread Tahini Sauce into the well. Spoon herbed chickpea mixture over the tahini. Top with remaining confit garlic cloves and aromatics. Finish with a drizzle of Confit Garlic Oil.
recipes.notes: For Basic Chickpeas: soak 200 g dried chickpeas overnight with 1 tsp baking soda. Drain, cover with water plus ½ tsp baking soda, boil 30-60 min until crushable. Add 1 tsp salt last 15 min.

recipes.name: Middle Eastern Bread Spread

ingredients.name: 4 pita breads, lightly toasted if desired
200 g block fresh cheese, such as feta, cut into ½-inch planks
1 small bunch radishes and fresh herbs such as mint or parsley, for serving

instructions: Make the Za'atar Oil. Set aside in a small bowl.
Grate tomatoes on the coarse side of a box grater. Transfer grated tomatoes to a fine-mesh sieve set over a bowl; drain 5-10 minutes. Discard tomato water.
Place grated tomatoes in a fresh bowl with 3 tbsp olive oil, garlic, and ¼ tsp salt. Stir and transfer to a serving bowl.
Slice pita into quarters and arrange on a platter. Place Za'atar Oil alongside the tomato and pita.
Arrange feta on the platter and drizzle with honey and remaining tbsp olive oil. Nestle radishes and fresh herbs alongside and serve.
recipes.notes: Dip bread in za'atar oil, spoon tomato over, eat with a nibble of cheese.

recipes.name: Labneh With Berries

ingredients.name: 10 g lemon thyme or thyme sprigs, plus a few extra picked leaves to serve
1 orange; 6 strips of skin finely shaved
300 g strawberries, hulled and halved lengthwise
