1 lime; 1 tbsp juice, 1 tsp finely grated zest
1½ tbsp sumac, plus extra to serve

instructions: Make the labneh 12-48 hours ahead.

Make the orange oil. Place olive oil in a small saucepan over medium-low heat and warm about 7 minutes or until tiny air bubbles form. Add thyme and orange strips, remove from heat, and infuse at least 30 minutes or overnight.
Make the berry topping. Add 1/3 each of blackberries, raspberries, and strawberries to a food processor with sugar, lime juice, and sumac. Blitz smooth, 1-2 minutes. Pour into a mixing bowl.
Add all remaining berries, blueberries, and cherries to a large bowl along with the blitzed fruit; stir gently.

To serve, spread labneh onto a large platter, smoothing with back of a spoon. Spoon berry mixture over labneh. Drizzle with 2 tbsp orange oil, top with orange strips and picked thyme. Sprinkle with lime zest and a pinch of sumac.
recipes.notes: Frozen berries work just as well. Extra orange oil keeps in a glass jar for salads.

recipes.name: Green Herb Shakshuka

ingredients.name: 800 g leeks (roughly 550 g once trimmed), washed and sliced in half lengthwise, then trimmed into ½-inch half-moons
10 garlic cloves, 7 crushed and 3 thinly sliced
2 tsp cumin seeds, toasted and finely crushed
100 g cilantro, roughly chopped in the food processor
60 g dill, roughly chopped in the food processor
100 g parsley, roughly chopped in the food processor
150 g (about 10) scallions, trimmed and thinly sliced
3 limes; juice from 2, plus 1 cut into wedges to serve

instructions: Make the Rose Harissa.

Add 5 tbsp olive oil to a large sauté pan over medium heat. Add leeks and ½ tsp salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until soft, about 15 minutes. Add crushed garlic and cumin, stirring until aromatic, 2-3 minutes. Add cilantro, dill, parsley, and scallions. Cook, stirring often, until fragrant and deep green, about 20 minutes.

Increase heat to medium-high and add spinach in batches, cooking down between additions. Add turmeric, 1 tsp salt, and pepper. Add 300 ml water; cook until liquid has almost evaporated, about 10 minutes. Stir in lime juice.
Make 8 wells in the green base. Crack an egg into each well; sprinkle with salt and pepper. Cover and cook 3-5 minutes over low heat until whites are set and yolks runny (longer if desired firmer).

While eggs cook, add remaining 3 tbsp oil to a small frying pan over medium-high heat. Once sizzling, add sliced garlic and cook until lightly golden, 1-2 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in Rose Harissa.
Spoon crispy garlic and harissa mixture all over the eggs. Serve immediately with lime wedges.
recipes.notes: Base can be made a day ahead. Serve with warm flatbread and labneh.

recipes.name: Roasted Eggplant Salad With Quick Lemon Paste and Quick-Pickled Chilies

ingredients.name: 20 g pistachios, lightly toasted and roughly chopped
2 lbs large Italian eggplants (about 3), trimmed and cut into 1-inch-thick rounds

instructions: Make the Quick Lemon Paste and Quick-Pickled Chilies.
Preheat oven to 180°C/350°F. Lightly toast pistachios about 6 minutes. Set aside.
Raise oven temperature to 200°C/400°F.

Toss eggplants in a large bowl with 4 tbsp oil, ¾ tsp salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a parchment-lined baking tray. Roast, turning halfway, until deeply golden and cooked through, 30-35 minutes. Cool.
In a large bowl, mix dill, parsley, basil, Quick Lemon Paste, maple syrup, a pinch of salt, and remaining 6 tbsp oil. Add cooled eggplant and toss until well coated.
Arrange eggplant on a plate and top with Quick-Pickled Chilies and chopped pistachios.

recipes.name: Grilled Carrots With Labneh and Dukkah

ingredients.name: 8 tbsp olive oil, plus 2 tsp olive oil

instructions: Make labneh 12-48 hours ahead. Make dukkah.
Wash and peel carrots; trim tops leaving 1 inch of green. Steam over boiling water until thickest part is easily pierced, about 10 minutes.
Make tarragon oil: blitz tarragon, 6 tbsp + 2 tsp oil, and a pinch of salt in a food processor until smooth, 2-3 minutes.
Toss steamed carrots with remaining 2 tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp salt, and pepper.
Place grill pan over high heat. Once smoking, grill carrots in batches, turning until lightly charred on all sides, 6-8 minutes.
Whisk honey and apple cider vinegar with a pinch of salt and pepper. Toss with grilled carrots.
Spread labneh onto a large platter with a well in the middle. Drizzle with tarragon oil, add carrots. Spoon dukkah over the carrots and serve more alongside. Drizzle with more tarragon oil.

recipes.name: Smacked Cucumber Salad With Sumac-Pickled Onions
instructions: Make the Sumac-Pickled Onions.
Toast sesame seeds in a medium frying pan over medium-high heat for 3-4 minutes. Set aside.
Trim tops and bottoms of cucumbers. Smack with the side of a knife until slightly bruised and breaking apart. Scoop seeds out and discard. Roughly chop into 1-inch pieces.
Transfer cucumbers to a bowl, season with 1 tsp salt, toss, and set aside 30 minutes. Drain through a fine-mesh strainer.
Meanwhile, make parsley oil: blitz parsley, garlic, ¼ tsp salt, and olive oil in a food processor until smooth.
Add drained cucumbers, Sumac-Pickled Onions, and a few tbsp parsley oil to a bowl; toss to combine. Transfer to a serving plate and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
recipes.notes: Leftover parsley oil keeps refrigerated up to 3 days.

recipes.name: Mafalda Pasta With Quick Shatta

ingredients.name: 4 tbsp Quick Shatta, plus extra to eat alongside
1 butternut squash (2 lbs), peeled, seeded, cut into 1-inch cubes
500 g full-fat Greek yogurt, at room temperature
5 g parsley leaves, roughly chopped, plus extra for garnish

instructions: Make the Quick Shatta.
Preheat oven to 230°C/450°F. Toss squash, onion, 3 tbsp oil, ¾ tsp salt, and pepper on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Roast, stirring halfway, until softened and charred, about 30 minutes.

Make fried garlic oil: add sliced garlic and 2 tbsp oil to a small pan off the heat, then place over medium heat. Cook gently until garlic is deeply golden and crispy, stirring occasionally, about 12 minutes. Set aside.

In a bowl, combine yogurt, cumin, cornstarch, egg yolks, 1 tbsp oil, and a pinch of salt. Pour into a large sauté pan over medium-low heat. Cook, stirring often, until thickened and just bubbling, about 15 minutes.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook pasta until almost al dente, ~6 minutes. Reserve 1 cup pasta water. Transfer pasta to yogurt sauce with reserved water; stir until smooth and creamy.
Stir in half the roasted squash and onion; taste for seasoning. Spoon remaining squash over the top.
Drizzle with shatta to taste; top with fried garlic oil. Sprinkle with parsley and remaining 1 tbsp olive oil.
recipes.notes: Don't mix cold yogurt with hot sauces too quickly or it may split — egg yolks and cornstarch stabilize.

recipes.name: Roasted Cauliflower With Harissa Chili Oil

ingredients.name: 2 large whole cauliflower with leaves (about 4 lbs)
360 g onion (1 large), peeled and cut into 8 wedges
8 Fresno chilies, stems on, slit down the center
15 tbsp olive oil, plus 1 tsp olive oil

instructions: Trim leaves at top of the cauliflower, exposing 2-3 inches of the head. Cut each cauliflower into quarters, keeping leaves attached at the base.
Fill a large pot with well-salted water; boil. Blanch cauliflower 2 minutes, weighting down with a lid. Transfer to a parchment-lined baking sheet. Add onion and Fresno chilies.
Preheat oven to 180°C/350°F. Make Rose Harissa.
Make chili oil: whisk Rose Harissa, tomato paste, Aleppo chili, sugar, garlic, salt, and olive oil.
Pour chili oil over cauliflower, onions, and Fresno chilies. Toss well (wear gloves), massaging chili oil into the crevasses.
Roast until cauliflower is golden brown and crispy, 45-60 minutes. Baste vegetables with chili oil 2-3 times during cooking.
Transfer to a serving platter, spoon over remaining chili oil and solids. Garnish with cilantro and lemon. Serve immediately.
recipes.notes: Chili oil keeps refrigerated up to 2 weeks. Optional: add unsalted butter to the sauce for non-vegan richness.

recipes.name: Salmon and Prawns in Spicy Tomato Sauce

ingredients.name: 9 tbsp olive oil, divided, plus 1 tsp olive oil
7 garlic cloves, 6 thinly sliced and 1 crushed
15 g (about 1½) dried ancho or cascabel chilies, stems and seeds removed and very roughly chopped
15 g cilantro, roughly chopped, plus 2 tbsp extra to serve
1 2½ lb side of salmon, skin and pin bones removed

instructions: Make the Tahini Sauce.

Add 4 tbsp oil to a large sauté pan over medium-high heat. Once hot, add sliced garlic and Fresno chilies; cook until fragrant and lightly colored, about 3 minutes. Add ancho/cascabel chilies, caraway seeds, and tomato paste. Cook, stirring, until tomato paste is deep red, about 1 minute.

Add fresh tomatoes, sugar, 1 cup water, and 1½ tsp salt. Bring to a simmer, lower heat to medium-low and cook, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes break down and sauce thickens slightly, about 12 minutes. Stir in cilantro, reserving about 1 tbsp for finishing oil.
Preheat oven to 220°C/400°F.
Season salmon with 1 tbsp oil and ¾ tsp salt. Season shrimp with 1 tbsp oil and ¼ tsp salt.

Transfer tomato sauce to a roasting tray. Place salmon skin-side down on top, tucking the tail underneath. Roast 10 minutes, then remove and nestle shrimp into the sauce, avoiding the top of the salmon. Return to oven until shrimp are just cooked, 3-5 minutes.

Make paprika oil: heat remaining 3 tbsp oil with crushed garlic and paprika in a small frying pan over medium-high until just bubbling and fragrant, 1-2 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in remaining cilantro.
Drizzle salmon generously with Tahini Sauce. Spoon paprika oil over top with a final drizzle of olive oil. Serve warm with extra tahini on the side.
recipes.notes: Sauce inspired by Tunisian/Libyan chreime, with a nod to prawns saganaki. Salmon can be swapped for trout or cod.

recipes.name: Celebration Rice With Saffron and Sweet Spiced Lamb

ingredients.name: 6 garlic cloves, peeled and roughly chopped
50 g ginger, peeled and roughly chopped
1 white onion, peeled and roughly chopped
20 g cilantro leaves and stalks, plus 5 g extra, chopped
150 g Greek-style yogurt, at room temperature
400 g basmati rice, washed and soaked 30 minutes to overnight

instructions: Preheat oven to 165°C/330°F. Pat lamb dry, season with ½ tsp salt and pepper. Heat oil in a large ovenproof saucepan or Dutch oven over medium-high; sear lamb until golden all over, ~10 minutes.
Blitz garlic, ginger, tomatoes, onion, jalapeños, and cilantro in a food processor until finely chopped.

Transfer lamb to a plate. Add the garlic-ginger mixture to the pan; cook over medium heat until fragrant and lightly colored, about 8 minutes. Add cumin, cinnamon, and allspice; cook 30 seconds. Return lamb with 4½ cups water, 1½ tsp salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil, cover, transfer to oven. Cook until tender, about 3 hours.
Uncover lamb, baste with juices, return to oven 30 more minutes (baste once halfway). Remove.

Make Saffron Water. In a large sauté pan over medium heat, melt 30 g butter with cloves and cinnamon sticks. Drain rice and add, stirring to coat. Add 3 cups boiling water and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a boil, cover tightly, lowest heat, undisturbed 15 minutes. Off heat, covered, rest 15 minutes.

Garnish: soak raisins, barberries, and cider vinegar at least 15 minutes. Melt 30 g butter in a frying pan over medium-high; add almonds and pinch of salt; cook until golden, 3-4 minutes. Off heat, stir in raisin mixture, cilantro, and parsley.
Stir saffron threads and soaking liquid gently into rice to leave streaks of yellow.
Transfer lamb and ⅔ of sauce to a bowl; shred into large pieces and remove bones. Whisk yogurt, parsley, and extra cilantro into remaining sauce in pan; transfer to a medium bowl.
Layer half the rice on a serving platter, top with half the lamb mixture. Repeat with remaining rice and lamb. Spoon nut garnish over. Serve with extra yogurt gravy alongside.
recipes.notes: Yotam's take on Iranian jeweled rice. Lamb neck can be swapped for shoulder, or pork shoulder.

recipes.name: Chicken Paillard with Sauce Vierge, Arugula & Pickled Red Onions
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II
instructions: Lay the chicken breast on plastic wrap, fold over, and pound to even thickness with the smooth side of a meat mallet.
Season both sides with kosher salt. Pour 1/8 inch canola oil into a sauté pan and heat over high until shimmering.

Lay chicken away from you, give the pan a shake. Reduce heat to medium-high and cook until browned, about 3 min. Flip and cook through, 5–6 min total, basting with hot oil. Done when slightly resistant to touch.
For pickled onions: bring 2:1:1 water:sugar:vinegar to a simmer until sugar dissolves; pour hot over sliced red onions in a canning jar. Refrigerate.
For sauce vierge: combine diced tomatoes and minced shallot in a bowl; coat with olive oil. Add Maldon salt, a drop of balsamic, and a squeeze of lemon. Mix gently.
For arugula salad: dress arugula lightly with olive oil and a sprinkle of salt; garnish with marcona almonds and pickled red onions; toss with a splash of balsamic.
Plate chicken, top with sauce vierge, serve salad alongside.
recipes.notes: Keller prefers kosher salt for cooking and Maldon or sel gris for finishing. Sautés in canola oil (high smoke point) rather than olive oil.

recipes.name: Wiener Schnitzel with German Potato Salad
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II

ingredients.name: trimmed veal top round, cut into 12 1/2-inch slices

instructions: Place veal in a food-grade plastic bag and pound with the spiked side of a mallet to 1/4-inch thickness. Refrigerate up to 12 hrs if making ahead.
Set up three breading bowls: 1/2-inch flour; eggs beaten with water to cream-like viscosity and seasoned with salt; 1/2-inch breadcrumbs (pulse panko fine if using).
Heat canola oil in sauté pan over high heat until shimmering.
Spritz cutlet with water, dredge in flour (pat off excess), dip in egg wash, coat in breadcrumbs. Fry about 1 min per side until golden. Drain on paper towels.
For mustard vinaigrette: whisk vinegar, mustards, and salt; slowly drizzle in canola oil while whisking to emulsify.
For potato salad: combine sliced shallots with 400g vinaigrette. Slice potatoes 3/16-inch on mandolin; simmer in cold salted water until just tender; fold gently into vinaigrette. Chill.
Slice cucumbers 1/8-inch; salt at 1% by weight 10 min; pat dry.
Bring potatoes to room temp; fold in cucumbers and parsley; top with crispy bacon and watercress.
Garnish schnitzel with lemon and parsley; serve with potato salad.
recipes.notes: Egg wash (not the meat) is seasoned generously. Spritzing the cutlet with water before flour creates the signature airy layer between meat and crust.

recipes.name: Buttermilk Fried Chicken with Braised Greens and Mashed Potatoes
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II
instructions: Make brine: combine all brine ingredients in 1 gal water, bring to boil, cool, and chill.
Cut chicken into 10 pieces with poultry shears. Brine in cold liquid 8–12 hrs (no longer).
Mix seasoned flour: flour, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, cayenne, salt.
Rinse, pat dry, and bring chicken to room temp. Set up dredging: seasoned flour, salted buttermilk, seasoned flour again.

Heat 2 inches peanut oil in cast iron to 325°F. Coat each piece: flour, buttermilk, flour. Fry dark meat first, then add white meat after 4 min. Maintain 325°F. Total ~11 min until 160–165°F internal.
Fry rosemary sprigs in oil at end until they stop sizzling.
Pulverize kosher salt and sprinkle over chicken; top with fried rosemary.

Braised greens: trim and wash greens. Heat canola oil in rondeau over medium; sweat bacon, onions, and salt until soft. Add garlic, then sugar and cider vinegar; reduce to syrup. Add chicken stock and greens gradually; cover and simmer 2 hrs until tender. Fold in halved cherry tomatoes.

Mashed potatoes: simmer unpeeled whole potatoes in cold water until very tender. Press through a ricer. Warm in saucepan over medium-low; incorporate hot cream in thirds and cubed butter to emulsify. Finish with clarified butter and salt.
recipes.notes: Served every other Monday at Ad Hoc. Do not over-brine — cured texture results past 12 hrs. Mashed potatoes are softer than potato purée (ricer vs. tamis).

recipes.name: Pan-Roasted Duck Breast with Braised Endive and Honey-Orange Gastrique
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II
instructions: Set duck breast skin-side up on a tray; air-dry uncovered in fridge 3 days.
Trim silver skin; prick skin densely with a sausage pricker to render fat.
Pan-roast: heat canola oil in 12-inch sauté pan over medium. Lay duck skin-side down; press lightly to crisp; do not move. At ~80% done, baste with rendered fat. Cook to 123°F internal (medium rare).

For endive: trim outer leaves to ~1.5 in, cut base flat, cone out the core. Pack inside and sprinkle outside with salt, rest 30 min, rinse. Brown in 1/4-inch canola oil; add orange juice to cover; top with parchment cartouche; simmer 30–40 min. Caramelize in duck fat just before serving.

For gastrique: simmer orange juice and honey to a syrupy consistency. Add veal stock and reduce by ~1/3. Stir in orange zest, lemon juice, salt; finish off heat with cold butter cubes for velvety texture.
Slice duck, fan on plate, position endive below, spoon gastrique around.
recipes.notes: Skin is air-dried 3 days for crispness. Endive can be made a week ahead, intensifies in its liquid.

recipes.name: Pan-Roasted Côte de Bœuf with Maître d'Hôtel Butter and Blanched Asparagus
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, room temp (for compound butter)

instructions: Truss the rib steak around its circumference using the bone as anchor. Salt both sides; air-dry uncovered on a rack 1 day.
Make maître d'hôtel butter: cream tempered butter; stir in parsley, lemon juice, salt. Roll in plastic wrap into a 4-inch log; chill until firm.
Bring steak to room temp 1 hr. Preheat oven 450°F. Heat cast-iron over high heat. Wrap bone in foil. Salt meat again. Add 3/8-inch canola oil; sear 4–5 min per side until crusty.
Pour off oil; add butter, thyme, crushed garlic. Baste meat in foaming butter. Transfer to oven 5 min, baste again, return 10–15 min until 130°F.
Rest 10–15 min. Remove twine; slice ribeye against grain into 1/4-inch slices. Sprinkle grey salt. Top with discs of compound butter; gently melt with kitchen torch.
For asparagus: peel/trim, bundle, blanch in heavily salted boiling water 2.5 min until tender. Drain.
recipes.notes: Air-drying overnight seasons the meat and removes surface moisture. Searing creates crust (does not seal in juice).

recipes.name: Brined Roast Chicken over Root Vegetables
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II
instructions: Make brine: combine ingredients in 1 gal water, bring to boil, cool, chill.
Remove neck/innards; cut out wishbone. Submerge chicken in cold brine 8–12 hrs.
Truss chicken. Air-dry trussed chicken uncovered in fridge 2 days.
Bring chicken to room temp 1.5–2 hrs.
Prep vegetables in 3/4-inch wedges; halve leeks lengthwise; halve carrots; toss with salt and clarified butter in roasting pan.
Preheat oven 475°F. Brush chicken with clarified butter; season skin with salt. Nest chicken in vegetables.
Roast 20–25 min; reduce to 400°F and roast 30–45 min until 160°F internal in thigh.
Rest 20–30 min. Reheat vegetables on stovetop; squeeze with lemon. Carve chicken over vegetables; finish with grey sea salt.
recipes.notes: Keller's signature roast chicken. Trussing improves browning evenness. Wishbone is removed for easier carving.

recipes.name: Blowtorch Prime Rib with Horseradish Cream, Glazed Carrots and Potato Purée
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II

ingredients.name: two-bone center-cut rib roast (~4.5 lbs), trimmed

instructions: Truss rib roast; salt all sides; air-dry uncovered on a rack in fridge overnight.
Position rack in lower third of oven; preheat to 275°F. Optionally score fat in 1/16-inch intervals.
Holding propane blowtorch ~1 inch from roast, brown all surfaces evenly until it looks roasted. Season generously with salt.
Roast about 2 hrs until 128°F internal. Rest 30 min — temperature will carry to 132°F.
Slice 1/2-inch thick; sprinkle with sel gris and pepper.
Horseradish cream: whip crème fraîche with horseradish to soft peaks; top with chives.
Glazed carrots: add carrots in single layer; sugar, water to barely cover, butter. Cook over high heat, swirling pan, until liquid forms a glaze. Add 2 drops vinegar if it breaks. Toss with parsley.
Potato purée: simmer whole unpeeled Yukon Golds until very tender. Pass through tamis. In saucepan over medium-low, incorporate 1/3 hot cream, then cubed butter; repeat. Drizzle in clarified butter.
recipes.notes: Propane (not butane) blowtorch is essential — it browns before cooking starts. Pink medium-rare can mislead — go by 128°F + carry-over.

recipes.name: Braised Pork Shoulder à la Matignon with Potato Rösti
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II

ingredients.name: Granny Smith apples, cored and diced

instructions: Make sachet: wrap bay leaf, cinnamon stick, star anise, and cloves in cheesecloth; tie.
Truss pork shoulder lengthwise then across width in 3 spots; bring to room temp; season all sides with kosher salt.
Preheat oven 275°F. Heat cocotte over medium-high; sear pork in 1/4-inch canola oil until well-browned. Transfer to rack.
In rendered fat, sauté onions with salt until caramelized. Add apples, celery root, sachet, most of the cider, and honey. Nestle pork in vegetables.
Cover; transfer to oven for ~4 hrs, checking after 2.5 hrs. Done when a cake tester slides in with no resistance.

Make rösti: peel and julienne potatoes on mandolin. Salt 5 min; squeeze in lint-free towel to dry. Toss with 2 tbsp clarified butter. Heat 8-inch pan with 3 tbsp clarified butter; add potatoes, compact to 1-inch even layer. Cook until edges brown; flip; cook 10–15 min until both sides crisp.
Remove pork and sachet to rest. Simmer braising liquid; grind kuzu and mix with reserved cider; whisk in to thicken. Season with vinegar, Calvados, salt.
Slice pork; ladle matignon onto plate; top with pork. Garnish with watercress; serve with rösti.
recipes.notes: Matignon vegetables (unlike mirepoix) are part of the finished dish. Replace cider with apple juice and omit honey if avoiding alcohol.

recipes.name: Red Wine Braised Short Ribs with Polenta and Mushroom Conserva
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II
instructions: Day 1: Bring red wine to simmer in saucepot. Add carrots, leeks, onions, garlic, and bouquet garni (parsley, thyme, bay, peppercorns). Burn off alcohol with blowtorch/lighter. Cool; combine with trimmed 7-oz short rib portions in sealed bag in container; refrigerate 12–16 hrs.
Day 2: Preheat oven 275°F. Strain meat and bouquet from marinade. Simmer marinade and skim impurities until clarified back to wine color.
Heat 1/4-inch canola oil; salt and flour short ribs; sear all sides until dark purple-brown.
Add clarified marinade, ribs, veal stock, chicken stock, and bouquet to pot. Cover with parchment cartouche; braise 3 hrs until cake tester slides through.
Transfer ribs and cooking liquid to ceramic dish; cover; refrigerate overnight.
Day 3: Strain cooking liquid through chinois. Place meat in sauté pan; add 1/3 liquid plus a splash of chicken stock; simmer, basting until glazed to sauce consistency. Finish with butter.
Mushroom conserva: clean and cut mushrooms; heat olive oil with herbs and Espelette to 170°F; add mushrooms 5 min. Off heat, stir in sherry vinegar and salt; steep 45 min.
Polenta: boil stock with garlic and salt. Stream in polenta; cook 17–20 min until dry, whisking often. Warm milk separately. Beat in butter and milk in quarters; season.
Plate polenta, top with glazed short ribs, garnish with cracked pepper, sel gris, chives. Serve conserva alongside.
recipes.notes: 3-day process: marinate, braise+chill, glaze+serve. Clarifying the marinade after burning off alcohol restores the vibrant wine color.

recipes.name: Hibachi Mixed Grill with Eggplant and Garlic Confit
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II

ingredients.name: boneless chicken breast, skin on (6–7 oz)

instructions: Start binchotan in chimney; add to hibachi base; cover with grates; open vents halfway.
Drizzle onions with oil, salt, and arrange on grill. Brush meats with oil and salt; grill, flipping for browning. Watch for flare-ups.
As each item finishes, transfer to platter; drizzle with olive oil and lemon; finish with sel gris. Top with charred onions.
For confit: wrap leek leaves, parsley, thyme, bay in cheesecloth as bouquet garni. Halve Chinese eggplants lengthwise; score crosshatch; salt 25 min flesh-down.
Lay eggplants flesh-down in baking dish with garlic and bouquet; heat oil to 250°F and ladle over to submerge.
Bake at 300°F about 45 min until creamy and tender.
Drain; plate with garlic; drizzle aged balsamic; sprinkle herbs and Maldon.
recipes.notes: Binchotan burns lower and longer than hardwood and imparts a clean woodsy flavor. Confit oil can be reused for vinaigrettes.

recipes.name: Roasted Veal Stock (Pressure Cooker)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II

ingredients.name: veal osso buco or meaty neck bones

instructions: Preheat oven 425°F (convection if available). Dry bones; cut meat off and slice 1/2-inch. Toss with oil; arrange in roasting pan; roast ~45 min to mahogany color, stirring at 30 min.
Heat pressure cooker over medium-high with 3 tbsp oil. Brûlée halved onion cut-side down ~10 min until black. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium; add diced tomatoes; cook until they caramelize and stop sizzling. Deglaze with water; re-caramelize.
Add roasted bones. Deglaze the roasting pan on stovetop with 1/2 L water; pour into pressure cooker.
Add brûléed onion, mirepoix vegetables, herbs, calf's foot. Add 3.5 L hot water to submerge. Seal; bring to 15 PSI; cook 90 min.
Release pressure naturally. Skim bones and vegetables out. Strain through China cap then through chinois.
Cool, refrigerate overnight, and skim solidified fat. Refrigerate 3 days or freeze 1 month.
recipes.notes: Pressure cooker method scales down the 3-day restaurant process. Stock steam-cooks so requires little skimming. Yields ~4 liters.

recipes.name: Light Chicken Stock
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II
instructions: Tie bouquet garni with leek leaves, parsley, thyme, and bay in cheesecloth.
Rinse bones and chicken feet under cold water, changing water until clear of blood.
Place bones in 12-qt stockpot; cover with cold water; slowly bring to a simmer (never boil). Skim impurities continuously, preserving the golden schmaltz at the surface.
Once simmering, add 2 qts ice (helps fat solidify); skim off fat and reserve.
Add vegetables, bay leaf, and bouquet garni; simmer 45 min, skimming frequently.
Strain through China cap into container; do not press solids. Strain again through fine chinois. Chill rapidly in ice bath.
Refrigerate; reboil after 3 days or freeze for longer storage.
recipes.notes: 45-minute simmer keeps the stock light and clear. Reserved schmaltz is great for roasting potatoes or making latkes.

recipes.name: Three Vinaigrettes: Emulsified, Sauce Vierge, and Chow Chow
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II
instructions: Emulsified vinaigrette: combine raw egg yolk, garlic, shallots, and thyme in a bowl. Drizzle in olive oil while whisking constantly to emulsify. Drizzle in balsamic. Add Dijon to taste.
Sauce vierge: combine diced tomatoes and minced shallot. Coat with EVOO. Fold in minced parsley; season with Maldon, balsamic, and lemon.
Pickled vegetables: combine cut vegetables in a jar with thyme, mustard seeds, and crushed garlic. Simmer water, vinegar, sugar; pour hot over vegetables; seal and chill.
Chow chow vinaigrette: chop pickled vegetables; combine with mustard, olive oil, shallots, and pickling liquid; mix gently. Squeeze lemon, season, finish with chives.
recipes.notes: Standard ratio is 3:1 oil:vinegar but Keller encourages experimentation. Emulsified version uses an egg yolk for body; mustard alone works without egg.

recipes.name: Chicken Velouté with Sauces Suprême, Allemande, and Albufera
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II
instructions: Beurre manié: mix equal parts butter and flour into a smooth paste.
Velouté: heat chicken stock to a simmer. Whisk in beurre manié gradually until sauce thickens to coat a spoon. Cook out off-center to drive impurities aside; skim; season.
Sauce suprême: whisk heavy cream and crème fraîche into velouté; season.
Sauce allemande: temper an egg yolk with hot velouté, return to pan whisking, do not boil. Strain through chinois; finish with lemon.
Sauce albufera: whisk veal stock and crème fraîche into velouté; season with kosher salt.
recipes.notes: Velouté is one of Escoffier's mother sauces. Use beurre manié for single-use sauce; make a shelf-stable oven-baked roux (110g butter + 110g flour at 250°F 1 hr) for batches.

recipes.name: Brown Chicken Quick Sauce and Sauce Chasseur
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II

ingredients.name: chicken parts: necks, backs, feet, cut to 1-inch
fines herbes: chervil, parsley, chives, tarragon

instructions: Bring bones to room temp. Heat canola oil in wide heavy pot until smoking. Add bones in single layer; sear 10 min without stirring. Turn; sear another 10 min until well-browned. Push bones aside; strain off most oil.
First deglaze: add tomatoes; reduce until paste-like and reglazed.
Second deglaze: add 1 cup water; scrape and reduce until reglazed.
Third deglaze: add chicken stock; reduce. Add mirepoix, sachet, and veal stock.
Offset pot over flame; skim impurities; simmer 30–45 min. Strain through China cap, then fine sieve. Cool, then press paper towel on surface to lift remaining fat.
Sauce chasseur: add 15g butter to saucier; sweat mushrooms with salt then shallots without browning. Add quick sauce; reduce by half. Stir in remaining butter, tomato concassé, and fines herbes.
recipes.notes: 'Quick' is relative — multi-hour reduction. Foundational technique adaptable to lamb, duck, venison, or veal bones.

recipes.name: Sous Vide Short Rib
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques II
instructions: Set immersion circulator to 62°C.
Salt both sides of short rib; vacuum seal in bag; submerge in bath. Cover bath with foil to retain heat.
Cook 48 hours.
Remove and pat dry. Heat thin oil in small sauté pan until smoking. Sear short rib 30 sec per side.
Add butter; reduce heat to medium; baste 30 sec.
Drain on paper towels. Slice on bias to serve.
recipes.notes: Alternate: 79°C for 24 hrs yields a traditionally braised texture. Experiment with thyme or peppercorns in the bag.

recipes.name: Chicken Paillard
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: 1 boneless, skinless chicken breast, about 5 ounces

instructions: Lay the chicken breast on a large sheet of plastic wrap and fold the plastic wrap over the meat. Pound to an even thickness using the smooth side of a meat mallet.
Season both sides with salt. Pour canola oil into a sauté pan, using enough so the layer of oil is about 1/8-inch deep. Heat over high heat.

When the oil is shimmering and gives off the first faint wisp of smoke, lay the chicken into the pan, working away from you. Shake the pan so the chicken does not stick. Reduce heat to medium-high to prevent burning.

Cook until the underside is browned, about 3 minutes. Flip and cook until cooked through and the second side is browned, about 5 to 6 minutes total. Spoon hot oil over the chicken to accelerate the cooking.
When the chicken has just a slight resistance to the touch, it is done. Plate with the accompaniments (pickled red onions, arugula salad, sauce vierge).
recipes.notes: Paillard technique can also be used for monkfish, beef tenderloin, or pork loin. Try sautéing fish in clarified butter instead of oil.

recipes.name: Pickled Red Onions (Keller)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: White wine vinegar (or vinegar of your choice)

instructions: Put the sliced red onions into a 16-oz canning jar.
Use a ratio of 2:1:1 — 2 parts water, 1 part sugar, 1 part vinegar. Combine in a saucepot and bring to a simmer.
Once the sugar has dissolved, pour the hot pickling liquid over the onions to submerge them. Seal the jar and refrigerate.

recipes.name: Keller Arugula Salad with Marcona Almonds
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Lightly dress the arugula with olive oil, using just enough that the leaves take on a light sheen. Toss.
Sprinkle with salt — the oil helps the salt cling to the arugula.
Garnish with Marcona almonds and pickled red onions and toss with balsamic vinegar.

recipes.name: Sauce Vierge (Keller)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Vinegar of your choice (balsamic or champagne)

instructions: Place diced tomatoes and minced shallots in a mixing bowl. Add enough olive oil to thoroughly coat and absorb into the tomatoes.
Gently fold in chopped parsley.
Season with Maldon salt, a drop of balsamic vinegar, and a squeeze of lemon juice.
recipes.notes: Created by Michel Guérard. Versatile — works on melted zucchini, salads, fish, eggs, or chicken paillard.

recipes.name: Wiener Schnitzel
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Trimmed veal top round, cut across the grain into 12 1/2-inch slices
Breadcrumbs (or panko pulsed in food processor)

instructions: Place each piece of veal in a large food-grade plastic bag and pound with the spiked side of a meat mallet to a uniform thickness of about 1/4 inch.

Set up a breading station with three bowls: about 1/2 inch flour in one shallow bowl; lightly beaten eggs diluted with water (viscosity of cream, seasoned generously with salt) in the second; 1/2 inch of breadcrumbs in the third.
Heat the canola oil in a 12-inch sauté pan over high heat until shimmering.
Working one at a time, spray the cutlet with water. Dip both sides in flour, patting off excess. Dip in egg, letting excess drip back. Coat both sides with breadcrumbs.
Add the dredged cutlet to the hot oil and cook about 1 minute per side until crisp and golden.
Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate. Plate with lemon wedges and parsley.
recipes.notes: Use one schnitzel per pan to avoid overcrowding. Look for non-confinement veal with little marbling.

recipes.name: Whole Grain Mustard Vinaigrette (Keller)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Combine the vinegar, mustards, and salt in a mixing bowl. Whisk well until combined.
Slowly drizzle in the canola oil while whisking vigorously until well emulsified.
Store refrigerated in an airtight container until needed.

recipes.name: German Potato Salad (Keller)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Slice shallots on a mandolin to 1/8-inch thick. Combine with the vinaigrette in a large mixing bowl.
Slice the Red Bliss and Yukon Gold potatoes to 3/16-inch thick. Rinse well and drain.
Place sliced potatoes in a large pot, cover with 1 inch of cold water, bring to a simmer, and cook lightly until just tender.
Transfer potatoes with a spider to the bowl and fold in the vinaigrette and shallots gently.
Cool in the refrigerator.
Slice cucumbers 1/8 inch thick, salt with 1% by weight, let sit 10 minutes, pat dry.
Let dressed potatoes come to room temperature. Fold in salted cucumbers and minced parsley. Garnish with chopped bacon and watercress.

recipes.name: Keller Fried Chicken
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Fleur de sel or fine sea salt

instructions: Mix all brine ingredients into 1 gallon of water and bring to a boil. Remove from heat, cool, and refrigerate until chilled.
Using poultry shears, cut the chicken into 10 pieces (2 wings, 2 legs, 2 thighs, 2 halved breasts). Brine for 12 hours (no longer).
Remove chicken from brine, rinse, pat dry, and let come to room temperature.
Combine all coating ingredients in a large bowl. Pour buttermilk into another bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Fill a cast-iron pan with 2 inches of peanut oil and heat to 325°F.
Dip each piece into coating, then buttermilk, then coating again. Transfer to parchment.
Start frying dark meat first; after 4 minutes, add white meat. Maintain 325°F. Fry about 7 more minutes until 160-165°F internal and golden brown.
Transfer to cooling rack, skin side up. Fry rosemary sprigs in the oil until they stop sizzling.
Pulverize kosher salt in a mortar to fine powder and sprinkle over chicken. Top with fried rosemary leaves.
recipes.notes: Never reuse brine. For Nashville-hot style, increase cayenne.

recipes.name: Keller Braised Greens
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Trim stems, cut leaves into 1 1/2-inch pieces, wash, and spin dry.
Heat canola oil in a rondeau over medium heat. Add bacon, onions, and salt; sweat until onions are translucent and bacon renders.
Add garlic and cook 2 minutes. Add sugar and vinegar, reduce to syrupy consistency.
Add 500g chicken stock and the greens gradually as they wilt. Cover and simmer over low heat for about 2 hours, adding more stock as needed.
Season with salt and vinegar. Fold in halved cherry tomatoes and serve.

recipes.name: Keller Mashed Potatoes
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Place whole, unpeeled potatoes in a 3-quart saucepot, cover with 2 inches cold water, slowly bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook until extremely tender when tested with a paring knife.
One at a time, remove from water and press through a ricer.
Transfer riced potatoes to a saucepan over medium-low heat. Incorporate 1/3 of hot cream, then a few cubes of butter, stirring with a stiff rubber spatula until butter emulsifies.
Drizzle in clarified butter. Continue adding cream, butter, and clarified butter to develop a light, fluffy consistency.
Season with salt, transfer to bowl, top with a pat of butter.
recipes.notes: Cooking potatoes whole prevents water absorption so more butter and cream can be incorporated.

recipes.name: Pan-Roasted Duck Breast
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Rinse and pat the duck breast dry. Set skin-side up on a baking sheet uncovered in the refrigerator for 3 days to dry the skin.
Trim silver skin. Prick the skin with a sausage pricker to allow fat to render (do not pierce flesh).
Heat sauté pan over medium heat with a thin layer of canola oil. Lay breast skin-side down, working away from you. Press with a palette knife where the skin needs more contact.
Cook gently. When 80% done, baste with rendered fat. Cook to medium rare (123°F internal).
When 90% done, pour off excess fat, add endive (if using), flip the breast to color the meat side briefly.
Transfer to a rack skin-side down to drain. Rest at least 5 minutes.
Slice and fan across the plate; serve with honey-orange gastrique and braised endive.
recipes.notes: Always source fresh duck if possible. Pekin breasts take well to pan-roasting; legs better suited to braising.

recipes.name: Honey-Orange Gastrique
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Put orange juice and honey in a medium saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat and reduce until syrupy.
Slowly add veal stock, return to simmer, and reduce by about a third.
Add orange zest. Adjust with lemon juice or vinegar to balance acid. Season with salt.
Off heat, stir in cold-cubed butter to soften flavors and add a velvety texture.
recipes.notes: Makes 240 g.

recipes.name: Braised Belgian Endive
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Cut off the bottoms of the endives so they stand. Remove conical core from the root end.
Pack the inside with kosher salt and sprinkle the outside. Let sit 30 minutes, then rinse.
Heat 1/4 inch canola oil in a pot large enough to hold endives in one layer. Lightly brown on all sides.
Add orange juice to cover, cover with a parchment cartouche, and simmer 30-40 minutes until fully cooked.
Set aside in liquid until ready to caramelize. If serving with duck, caramelize in the pan with rendered duck fat.
recipes.notes: Can be made up to one week in advance and refrigerated in the cooking liquid.

recipes.name: Côte de Bœuf (Pan-Roasted Rib Steak)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Double-cut rib steak, about 2 to 2 1/2 pounds

instructions: Truss the steak around the circumference with kitchen twine, using the bone as anchor. Salt both sides and air-dry uncovered in the refrigerator for 1 day.
One hour before cooking, bring to room temperature. Pat dry.
Heat oven to 450°F. Wrap the bone in foil. Heat 3/8 inch canola oil in a cast-iron skillet over high heat until wafting smoke.
Season meat again with salt and add to pan. Sear 4-5 minutes until dark brown and crusty. Flip and brown second side 2-3 minutes.
Pour off most of the oil. Add a small amount of fresh oil plus cold-cubed butter, thyme, and garlic. Baste the meat with butter and pan juices.
Transfer to 450°F oven for 5 minutes, baste again, then return to oven for 10-15 minutes until thermometer reads 130°F for medium-rare.
Rest 10-15 minutes. Slice off the bone, slice the ribeye against the grain, and continue with the deckle. Sprinkle with grey salt.
Top with discs of maître d'hôtel butter and gently warm with kitchen torch to melt.
recipes.notes: Côte de bœuf is a celebratory cut for sharing — the deckle is Keller's favorite section.

recipes.name: Maître d'Hôtel Butter
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Stir the tempered butter in a small bowl until smooth. Add remaining ingredients and stir to combine.
Form into a compact log about 1 1/4 inches in diameter on plastic wrap, twist ends, and tie. Refrigerate to firm before slicing into discs.
recipes.notes: Can be stored in fridge for a few days or frozen up to 2 months.

recipes.name: Big-Pot Blanched Asparagus
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Peel the spiky tips along the stalk with a paring knife. Snap off the fibrous bottom.
Fill a stockpot with water to within a few inches of the top. Add enough salt to make it as salty as seawater.
Bundle and tie 6 to 7 asparagus spears. Place bundles in boiling water in batches.
After 2 1/2 minutes, check doneness with paring knife. Continue cooking until tender. Cut twine and arrange on a platter.

recipes.name: Keller Roast Chicken with Root Vegetables
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Make brine: mix all brine ingredients with 1 gallon water, bring to boil, cool.
Cut wishbone out of chicken. Brine 8 to 12 hours.
Truss the brined chicken, then air-dry uncovered in the refrigerator for 2 days.
Bring chicken to room temperature (1 1/2 to 2 hours).
Cut rutabagas into 3/4-inch wedges; cut turnips similarly. Halve and rinse leeks; halve carrots and parsnips. Cut onion into wedges; leave potatoes whole.
Combine vegetables in roasting pan, season with salt, drizzle with clarified butter or canola oil.
Preheat oven to 475°F. Brush chicken with clarified butter and season with salt. Nestle in vegetables.
Roast 20-25 minutes at 475°F, then reduce to 400°F and roast 30-45 minutes until 160°F in the thigh.
Rest 20-30 minutes. Reheat vegetables in pan juices on stovetop. Finish with a squeeze of lemon. Carve chicken and arrange over vegetables. Finish with grey sea salt.
recipes.notes: Method also works for turkey, pigeons, guinea fowl, or quail — preserve salt-to-water ratio.

recipes.name: Blowtorch Prime Rib Roast
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Two-bone center-cut rib roast, about 4 1/2 pounds, trimmed of excess fat
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

instructions: Position oven rack in lower third and preheat to 275°F. Place trussed rib roast on a rack in a roasting pan.
Optionally score the fat in 1/16-inch intervals. Hold a blowtorch about an inch from the roast and lightly brown the white fat and red meat on all sides.
Season generously with salt.
Roast 2 hours or until internal temperature reaches 128°F. Rest at least 30 minutes — it will rise to 132°F for medium-rare.
Carve away the bones and slice into 1/2-inch slices. Sprinkle with sel gris and pepper.
recipes.notes: Score skin and torch for instant browning without losing slow-roast tenderness.

recipes.name: Horseradish Cream (Keller)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Combine crème fraîche and horseradish and whip until soft peaks form (over ice if needed for cold).
Top with minced chives.
recipes.notes: Can be made up to a week in advance; add chives just before serving.

recipes.name: Keller Glazed Carrots
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Sweet or fresh garden carrots, peeled, oblique cut

instructions: Place carrots in a single layer in a saucepot. Add sugar and enough water to barely cover. Add butter and turn heat to high.
Move pan to keep carrots evenly spaced. Listen for the water to crackle as it evaporates.
Reduce heat to medium and continue until butter emulsifies into a shiny glaze and carrots are just tender.
If glaze breaks, add a little water and two drops of white wine vinegar to re-emulsify.
Toss with chopped parsley. Sprinkle with finishing salt.

recipes.name: Pommes Purée (Keller Potato Purée)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Place whole, unpeeled potatoes in a saucepot, cover with 2 inches cold water, bring to gentle simmer. Cook until extremely tender.
One at a time, halve and press the flesh through a tamis with a stiff bowl scraper, leaving skins behind.
Transfer to a 4-quart saucepan over medium-low heat. Incorporate 1/3 of hot cream, then beat in cubes of butter until emulsified. Drizzle in clarified butter.
Continue adding cream, butter, and clarified butter to develop a creamy purée. Add hot water to restore emulsion if it breaks.
Season with salt and top with a pat of butter.
recipes.notes: Differs from mashed potatoes by using a tamis instead of a ricer for a silkier texture.

recipes.name: Pork Shoulder à la Matignon
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Granny Smith apples, cored and 3/8-inch dice
French grey sea salt, for finishing

instructions: Make sachet: lay cheesecloth flat, add bay leaf, cinnamon, star anise, cloves. Roll and tie with twine.
Bring pork to room temperature 1 hour before cooking. Truss with twine. Season all sides with salt.
Preheat oven to 275°F. Heat 1/4 inch canola oil in a large cocotte. Sear pork on all sides until well browned. Remove to a rack.
Add onions to the cocotte; salt to draw moisture and caramelize. Add apples and celery root.
Add the sachet and most of the cider (reserve some for slurry). Step away from steam. Stir in honey.
Nestle pork into the bed of vegetables. Cover and cook 30 seconds, then transfer cocotte to oven for about 4 hours, checking at 2 1/2 hours with a cake tester.
Remove pork and sachet. Bring the remaining liquid to a simmer. Grind kuzu and whisk into reserved cider to make a slurry; stir into the simmering liquid in thirds to thicken.
Taste; add Calvados, adjust salt and vinegar. Slice pork and serve over the matignon. Garnish with watercress and serve with potato rösti.
recipes.notes: Technique works with lamb shanks, osso buco, oxtail, or pot roast. Without alcohol, use apple juice and omit honey.

recipes.name: Potato Rösti (Keller)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Peel potatoes, slice lengthwise on a mandolin, then julienne lengthwise. Toss with salt and let wilt 5 minutes. Squeeze in a lint-free towel to release moisture.
Toss grated potatoes with 2 tablespoons clarified butter. Heat 8-inch sauté pan over medium-high heat. Add 3 tablespoons clarified butter.
When butter just begins to smoke, add the potatoes. Compact tightly with a cake spatula into an even 1-inch-thick layer.
When rösti browns around the edges, peek bottom and adjust heat. When golden brown, flip carefully with a wide spatula.
Pour remaining butter around perimeter. Reduce to medium-low and cook 10-15 minutes until other side is well-browned and crisp.
Loosen edges, slide onto serving dish, sprinkle with chives, and cut into wedges.
recipes.notes: Can be embellished with bacon, leeks, garlic, or minced onions.

recipes.name: Red Wine Braised Short Ribs
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Boneless short ribs, 7 oz each (210 g)

instructions: Marinade: simmer wine with mirepoix and bouquet garni; burn off alcohol with blowtorch. Cool and chill.
Day 1: Trim and portion meat. Marinate in chilled marinade 12-16 hours.
Day 2: Preheat oven to 275°F. Remove meat and bouquet garni. Bring marinade to simmer in saucepan and clarify by skimming until vibrant.
Heat 1/4 inch canola oil in a sauté pan. Season and dredge meat in flour. Sear 2-3 minutes per side until dark brown with a purple tint.
Transfer meat to paper towels. Pour off oil; return clarified marinade to pan. Add short ribs, veal stock, light chicken stock, and bouquet garni. Cover meat with liquid.
Bring to simmer. Cover with parchment cartouche and braise in oven about 3 hours until a cake tester slides through easily.
Transfer meat and liquid to baking dish. Cool, cover, rest overnight in refrigerator.

Day 3: Strain braising liquid through chinois. Place meat in sauté pan with 1/3 of strained liquid and a couple ounces light chicken stock. Bring to simmer, basting and glazing. Finish sauce with butter.
recipes.notes: Use cake tester for doneness, not time. Can be reduced/applied to beef cheeks, lamb shanks, veal, or used with chicken for coq au vin.

recipes.name: Mushroom Conserva (Keller)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Extra virgin olive oil (enough to cover mushrooms)

instructions: Clean mushrooms and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Combine olive oil with herbs and chile flakes. Heat oil to 170°F, add mushrooms, stir, return to 170°F. Cook 5 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in vinegar and salt. Steep 45 minutes.
Transfer to a clean container. Refrigerate up to 1 week.

recipes.name: Polenta with Whole Milk and Butter (Keller)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Extra virgin olive oil, to finish

instructions: Combine stock, garlic, and salt in a large saucepan and bring to a boil.
Pour in polenta in a stream and cook over low heat, whisking often, 17-20 minutes until quite dry and coating the bottom of the pan.
Warm milk in a small saucepan.
Increase heat under polenta to medium and stir in butter. Add milk a quarter at a time, letting polenta absorb each addition. Season to taste.
Spoon into serving dish; top with short ribs; finish with cracked pepper, sel gris, and chives. Serve mushroom conserva alongside.

recipes.name: Hibachi Mixed Grill (Steak, Lamb Chops, and Chicken)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Lamb chops, single bone, about 4 to 5 ounces
Boneless chicken breast, skin on, 6-7 ounces
Beef sirloin, 5-6 ounce pieces, about 1 inch thick

instructions: Light binchotan in a chimney starter following manufacturer instructions. Add to hibachi base; cover with grates and set vents about halfway open.
Drizzle onions with oil, season with salt, arrange on grill.
Brush meats with oil and season with salt. Arrange on the grill. Keep a spray bottle nearby for flare-ups.
Each item cooks at a slightly different rate. Look for browning and flip; test for doneness by touch.
Transfer each to a platter as it finishes. Drizzle with olive oil, squeeze lemon, sprinkle sel gris, top with charred onions.
Serve with eggplant and garlic confit.
recipes.notes: Binchotan hardwood charcoal burns hotter than briquettes — Keller's preferred fuel.

recipes.name: Roasted Veal Stock (Keller)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Veal osso bucco or meaty neck bones

instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (use convection if available).
Dry the bones, cut meat away, slice into 1/2-inch pieces. Toss in oil, arrange in a single layer in a roasting pan.
Roast about 45 minutes until deeply mahogany, stirring at 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the pressure cooker over medium-high with about 3 tablespoons oil. Brûlée halved onion cut-side down until charred black (10 minutes).
Remove charred onion. Reduce heat. Add diced tomatoes and cook until they caramelize and stop sizzling. Deglaze with a little water and re-caramelize.
Add roasted bones to pressure cooker. Deglaze roasting pan with 1/2 liter water and pour jus into cooker.
Add brûléed onion, mirepoix, herbs, calf's foot (if using), and 3 1/2 liters hot water. Stir, seal, bring to 15 PSI.
Maintain 15 PSI for 90 minutes. Release pressure naturally.
Remove bones and vegetables with skimmer. Strain through a China cap, then chinois into a clean container. Cool overnight in ice bath or refrigerator.
Remove solidified fat. Use or freeze.
recipes.notes: Stovetop alternative: simmer uncovered about 8 hours, doubling water and skimming impurities.

recipes.name: Light Chicken Stock (Keller)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Leeks, white and light green, 1-inch chunks

instructions: Make bouquet garni by wrapping leek leaves, parsley sprigs, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves in cheesecloth and tying.
Rinse bones, necks, backs, and feet under cold water until no traces of blood remain.
Place bones and feet in a 12-quart stockpot, cover with cold water, slowly bring to a simmer. Do not boil.
Skim impurities. Once simmering, add 2 quarts ice, turn off heat, and skim the golden fat (schmaltz) to reserve.
Add remaining vegetables and bouquet garni; slowly return to a simmer for 45 minutes, skimming often.
Strain through a China cap into a clean container without pressing solids. Then strain again through a fine chinois.
Chill in ice bath, refrigerate. Remove solidified fat before use. Reboil after 3 days or freeze.
recipes.notes: Reserved schmaltz can be heated to evaporate water; use to roast potatoes or make latkes.

recipes.name: Emulsified Vinaigrette (Keller)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Combine egg yolks, mustard, shallots, and thyme leaves in a mixing bowl.
Begin drizzling oil while whisking constantly until ingredients emulsify.
Drizzle in vinegar and continue whisking. Taste and adjust.
recipes.notes: Mustard can act as binding agent if avoiding raw egg. Stores in sealed container for a week.

recipes.name: Chow Chow Vinaigrette
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Jingle bell peppers (or other small variety)

instructions: Pickle: Cut vegetables to uniform size and add to a canning jar. Combine water, vinegar, sugar, thyme, mustard seeds, and garlic in a saucepot; bring to a simmer. Pour hot pickling liquid over vegetables and seal. Refrigerate.
Vinaigrette: Remove pickled vegetables from jar and chop. Place in bowl with mustard, olive oil, shallots, and pickling liquid; mix gently.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice and salt. Garnish with chives.

recipes.name: Chicken Velouté and Mother Sauces (Suprême, Allemande, Albufera)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III
instructions: Beurre manié: Mix equal parts butter and flour until smooth.
Velouté: Heat stock to simmering. Whisk in beurre manié (about half) to thicken. Offset pot from flame to drive impurities from flour to one side. Continue whisking; season to taste.
Sauce suprême: Whisk cream and crème fraîche into velouté; season.

Sauce allemande: Add an egg yolk to a mixing bowl. Temper with hot velouté, then slowly stream back into velouté while whisking. Do not boil. Strain through a fine chinois. Finish with a squeeze of lemon.
Sauce albufera: Whisk veal stock and crème fraîche into velouté. Season with salt.
recipes.notes: Velouté is one of the five French mother sauces. Roux alternative: bake butter-flour paste at 250°F for 1 hour to make a shelf-stable, low-flavor roux.

recipes.name: Brown Chicken Quick Sauce
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Chicken parts: necks, backs, feet, cut into 1-inch pieces

instructions: Bring bones to room temperature. Heat canola oil in a wide, heavy pot until smoking. Add bones in a single layer and sear about 10 minutes without stirring.
Turn and cook another 10 minutes until well-browned. Push bones to one side and strain off most of the oil.
First deglaze: add tomatoes, scrape the fond. Cook until liquid evaporates and the pan reglazes.
Second deglaze: add 1 cup water. Scrape and reduce again.
Third deglaze: add chicken stock and repeat. Add mirepoix, sachet, and veal stock.
Offset pan over flame to push impurities to one side. Skim and simmer 30-45 minutes.
Remove bones, sachet, and large vegetables. Strain through China cap, then fine mesh sieve into bowl set over ice bath. Press a paper towel onto surface to remove remaining fat.
recipes.notes: Yields 5 cups. Reduce to flavor, not consistency.

recipes.name: Sauce Chasseur
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Small button mushrooms, cleaned and quartered
Dry white wine (Sauvignon Blanc or white Burgundy)
Fines herbes (equal parts chervil, parsley, chives, tarragon, minced)

instructions: Add 15 g butter to a saucier over low heat. Add mushrooms and salt them to draw out moisture.
Add shallots and sweat 1 minute without coloring.
Add wine and deglaze. Simmer until almost dry (au sec).
Ladle in chicken quick sauce; reduce by half. Turn heat to low, stir in remaining butter.
Add tomato concassé and fines herbes. Stir to combine and serve.

recipes.name: Sous Vide Short Rib (Keller)
recipes.source: Thomas Keller MasterClass — Cooking Techniques III

ingredients.name: Boneless short rib, approximately 210 g, about 1 inch thick

instructions: Prepare a water bath with an immersion circulator at 62°C.
Season short rib on both sides with salt. Vacuum seal and place in water bath. Cover with foil.
Cook 48 hours.
Remove and pat dry. Heat a small sauté pan with a thin coat of oil over high heat. When smoking, sear each side about 30 seconds.
Add butter, lower heat to medium, and baste about 30 seconds.
Transfer to paper-towel-lined plate to drain briefly. Slice on a bias and serve.
recipes.notes: Alternative: 79°C for 24 hours mimics traditional braised texture.

recipes.name: Crispy Whole Fried Branzino with Thai Chili Lettuce Cups
recipes.source: Gordon Ramsay MasterClass — Cooking II: Elevated Home Recipes
instructions: Heat 1 1/2 inches of vegetable oil to 350-360°F. Cut fins and tail off the fish with scissors.
Cut 1/3-inch deep down both sides of the vertebrae. Make 4-5 diagonal slices into the flesh, all the way to the ribs.
Combine garlic, ginger, shallots, lemongrass, Thai chilis, Shaoxing wine, fish sauce, honey, and rice wine vinegar. Marinate at least 1 hour.
Place branzino in a baking dish. Brush marinade inside the cavity, into the cuts, and onto the skin. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine cornstarch and rice flour. Sift over both sides of the fish. Stand the fish on its belly with the flaps spread.
Use a spider to lower fish into hot oil. Shallow fry until deep golden brown and very crispy, 8-10 minutes, ladling oil over exposed flesh.
Drain on a wire rack; season with salt.
Dipping sauce: stir together fish sauce, lime juice, sliced Thai chilis, brown sugar, and minced garlic. Chill.
Pickles: heat water, sugar, vinegar in saucepot. Add ginger and carrot pickles first, soak 20 min. Pour cooled liquid over cucumbers and mango. Chill 1 hour.
Lettuce cups: trim into 3-4 inch circles using kitchen scissors. Reserve in stacks.
Plate: place fried branzino on platter; fill lettuce cups with chiffonade lettuce, pickles, scallions, and a teaspoon of Thai dipping sauce. Arrange around the fish.
recipes.notes: Substitute cod, snapper, or bass if branzino is unavailable. Shaoxing wine can be replaced with dry sherry.

recipes.name: Raspberry Soufflé (Gordon Ramsay)
recipes.source: Gordon Ramsay MasterClass — Cooking II: Elevated Home Recipes
instructions: Raspberry purée: add raspberries, sugar, and water to a saucepot over medium-low heat. Cover and steam 5-8 minutes. Remove lid and reduce 5 minutes until syrupy.
Blend, then strain through a sieve. Reserve 100 g chilled for the soufflé base; keep the rest warm for garnish.

Pastry cream: warm milk over medium heat 3-5 minutes until scalding. Whisk yolks, sugar, cornstarch, and vanilla in a bowl. Temper by adding scalded milk slowly. Return mixture to saucepot and whisk over medium heat until thick and creamy.
Transfer to plastic-wrap-lined pan; lay another sheet directly on the surface and chill 30 min minimum.
Brush ramekins with a thin layer of butter; chill 30 seconds. Brush another thin layer, add shaved chocolate, and roll to coat sides.
Preheat oven to 355°F. Whisk together pastry cream and raspberry purée.
Whisk egg whites at medium speed. Once foaming, squeeze a small amount of lemon juice. When volume increases 2/3, stream in sugar. Whisk to stiff, glossy peaks.
Fold 1/3 meringue into pastry cream-purée mixture until smooth, then gently fold in the rest in two parts.
Fill ramekins to the top; tap to level. Scrape tops flat with offset spatula. Run thumb around the inside edge.
Bake 2 ramekins at a time on the center rack. 10-oz ramekins: 14-17 minutes; 6-oz ramekins: 10-12 minutes.
Dust with powdered sugar. For a formal presentation, poke two holes in the center and pour fresh raspberry coulis in before serving.
recipes.notes: Frozen raspberry purée (Boiron brand) is a fine substitute. Try other fruit purées like apricot or banana.

recipes.name: Roast Delicata Squash
instructions: Cut off the ends of the Delicata squash and peel the skin (skin is edible).
Cut in half lengthwise, scrape out seeds, then slice into 1-inch half moons.
Toss with olive oil, salt and pepper, and torn Kaffir lime leaves.
Spread evenly on a baking sheet and roast at 375°F for 40 minutes, until tender and lightly browned, stirring occasionally.
recipes.notes: From Chez Panisse Vegetables. Other vegetables to roast: winter squash, summer squash, potatoes, carrots, cabbage, cauliflower, fennel, Brussels sprouts, asparagus, onions, parsnips.

recipes.name: Steamed Tokyo Turnips

ingredients.name: Vinegar, soy sauce, or lemon juice (optional)

instructions: Separate the turnips and greens, leaving an inch of pale green stalks at the top.
Rinse the turnips well to remove grit, leave whole or cut into halves or quarters.
Wash the greens and discard any yellow or damaged leaves.
Place a steamer basket in a saucepan with a tight-fitting lid, add water to a depth of half an inch, and bring to a boil.
Add the turnips and greens to the basket, cover, and cook until just tender, 5 to 8 minutes depending on size.
Serve with salt and butter, drizzle of olive oil, dash of vinegar or soy sauce, or squeeze of lemon.
recipes.notes: From In the Green Kitchen. Other vegetables to steam: spinach, asparagus, mustard greens, corn, broccolini, baby bok choy.

recipes.name: Julienned Carrot Salad with Cumin Salt
instructions: Peel the carrots and julienne (a Japanese mandoline works quickly).
Mash the garlic clove with the cumin salt to a smooth paste and mix with the red wine vinegar.
Whisk in olive oil. Taste for seasoning and add more vinegar or salt if needed.
Toss with the carrots and add the chopped parsley.
recipes.notes: From Chez Panisse Vegetables. Variation: add cayenne and chopped cilantro.

recipes.name: Yogurt Raita

ingredients.name: Small garlic clove, pounded to puree

instructions: In a small bowl, whisk together all the ingredients.
Taste for salt and adjust.
recipes.notes: Variations: add grated cucumber; instead of chile flakes use pounded nigella, cumin or coriander; grate in ginger and carrot.

recipes.name: Brown Rice with Cilantro
instructions: Heat olive oil in a cast-iron pan and sauté cooked brown rice.
Season with salt and add chopped cilantro just before serving.
Taste for salt, and adjust if needed.
recipes.notes: Variations: mix with sautéed greens and serve with egg; add sautéed onion, garlic, almonds, currants for jeweled rice; or roll with avocado/cucumber/sesame in nori for a sushi-style cone.

recipes.name: Garlic Vinaigrette
instructions: Pound peeled garlic clove with 2 big pinches of salt in mortar and pestle into a very smooth paste.
Add the vinegar, grind in black pepper, and taste for the balance of salt and vinegar.
Allow to macerate for 10 to 15 minutes.
Whisk in olive oil. Taste with a leaf of lettuce; it should taste bright and lively without being too acidic or too oily. Adjust salt, vinegar, or oil as needed.
recipes.notes: Adapted from In the Green Kitchen.

recipes.name: Cumin Salt
instructions: Toast the cumin seeds in a hot cast-iron skillet, shaking the pan for even toasting until they pop and lightly brown.
Transfer the seeds to a mortar and pestle and pound with the salt until coarsely ground.
recipes.notes: From My Pantry.

recipes.name: Mexican Tortilla Soup

ingredients.name: Chicken breast half (with skin and bones)
Anaheim green pepper, seeded and thinly sliced
Crumbled queso fresco or grated Monterey Jack

instructions: Heat the chicken broth to a simmer, then add the chicken breast. Simmer until cooked, about 20 minutes. Transfer to a plate, cool, then discard skin and bones and shred the meat.
Heat peanut or vegetable oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat and fry tortilla strips in small batches until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels and season with salt.
In a large heavy pot, heat the olive oil and add green pepper, onion, garlic, and salt. Cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the hot broth, then add tomatoes, chipotle chile, and additional salt. Bring to a boil and simmer 30 minutes.
Add shredded chicken and oregano and heat through without boiling. Adjust salt.
Serve with crispy tortilla strips and small bowls of garnishes.
recipes.notes: From The Art of Simple Food.

recipes.name: Moroccan-Style Braised Vegetables
instructions: Drain the chickpeas and place in a medium pot with water to cover by 1.5 inches. Add onion, cinnamon stick, chile, 2 tbsp olive oil, and salt. Simmer until tender, about 45 minutes. Cool in liquid.
Preheat oven to 400°F. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Peel and halve carrots and cut into quarters. Cook carrots and turnips separately until just tender, about 5 minutes.
Peel and seed squash, cut into 1-inch chunks. Toss with oil and salt on a baking sheet, roast until tender, 15 to 20 minutes.
Lightly toast cumin, coriander, and saffron, then grind. Stir in turmeric and cayenne.
In a large skillet, warm olive oil. Add onion, celery, salt. Cook 5 minutes. Drain and dice tomatoes, add and cook 2 minutes.
Add spices, garlic, and ginger. Cook 2 minutes more. Add chickpeas with cooking liquid, simmer. Add squash, carrots, and turnips. Add water if needed.
Taste for salt and simmer 5 minutes. Serve with buttered couscous or saffron rice and harissa.
recipes.notes: From In the Green Kitchen. Pair with harissa.

recipes.name: Harissa
instructions: Toast 5 dried ancho chiles on a hot griddle until puffed and fragrant.
Cover with boiling water, soak for 20 minutes, drain.
Roast, peel, and seed 1 large red bell pepper.
In a blender or food processor, purée the drained chiles and peeled pepper with garlic, olive oil, red wine vinegar, and salt.
Thin with water if desired.
recipes.notes: From In the Green Kitchen.

recipes.name: Spicy Indian Cauliflower Stems
instructions: Toast peppercorns, cardamom seeds, cassia, and cloves in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat until fragrant. Cool and grind to a powder.
Peel woody outer parts from cauliflower cores and stems, cut into large dice or thick slices.
Heat oil and cumin seeds in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook until cumin crackles, then add the stems.
Season with salt, toss, then cover tightly, reduce heat to low, and cook until tender.
Check and stir, letting condensation from the lid run back into the pan.
As cauliflower turns tender, season with ground spice mixture and mango powder. Stir to coat. Taste for salt.
recipes.notes: From The Art of Simple Food II.

recipes.name: Spiced Pears

ingredients.name: Firm Bosc, Bartlett or d'Anjou pears

instructions: Pour wine, sugar, and water into a saucepan and stir over low heat until sugar is dissolved.
Remove lemon zest, cut into julienne, and add to syrup with lemon juice.
Scrape vanilla bean seeds into syrup and add the bean. Add pears and simmer gently until tender, about 30 minutes.
Remove pears. Over high heat, reduce poaching liquid to about 1 cup. Add cream, lower heat, simmer 5 minutes. Strain and keep warm.
Crush the cinnamon sticks, cloves, star anise, and peppercorns coarsely.
Melt honey and butter together in a large sauté pan. Add pear pieces, sprinkle with spice mixture, and sauté over high heat until browned.
Arrange pears on plates and drizzle with sauce. Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.
recipes.notes: From Chez Panisse Fruit.

recipes.name: Coming Home Pasta
instructions: Toss hot spaghetti with a heap of minced garlic sautéed gently in olive oil.
Add dried chile flakes, a salted anchovy or two, a handful of chopped parsley, and salt to taste.
Enjoy with a glass of red wine.
recipes.notes: Alice and her daughter Fanny call this 'coming home pasta'.

recipes.name: Quick Pickling Brine
instructions: Combine all the ingredients in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Add small or chopped vegetables to the brine, cooking each type separately and removing when cooked but still slightly crisp.
Set vegetables aside to cool to room temperature. Allow brine to cool.
Gently stir vegetables together, transfer to jars, cover with cooled brine, and refrigerate.
recipes.notes: From My Pantry. Makes about 3 cups.

recipes.name: Broccoli Rabe with Garlic and Hot Pepper

ingredients.name: Dried cayenne pepper or pinch of chile flakes

instructions: Stem the broccoli rabe; cut off and discard woody parts. Cut stems into pieces; slice leaves into ribbons.
Wash greens in cold water and drain.
Add olive oil to a wide sauté pan over medium heat. When hot, add pepper or chile flakes and garlic. Stir once, then toss in broccoli rabe and salt.
Cook 4 to 12 minutes, adding water if pan gets too dry.
Just before serving, stir in extra-virgin olive oil.
recipes.notes: From The Art of Simple Food.

recipes.name: Ricotta, Honey, and Hazelnut Dessert
instructions: Cut a wedge of tender ricotta and layer a spoonful of just-warmed honey on top.
Finish with a sprinkle of toasted chopped hazelnuts.
recipes.notes: An opportunity to showcase a special honey.

recipes.name: Homemade Ricotta
instructions: Heat the milk in a heavy-bottomed nonreactive pot over medium heat until 190°F, stirring now and then.
Pour in vinegar, stir briefly, bring back up to 190°F.
Turn off heat and let sit undisturbed for 10 minutes.
Place a sieve over a large bowl, line with cheesecloth, gently ladle curds into cloth-lined sieve.
Slowly stir in salt. Drain a few minutes.
Eat right away or refrigerate up to 4 days.
recipes.notes: From My Pantry. Makes about 1.5 cups.

recipes.name: Oat Pancakes

ingredients.name: Ghee, coconut oil, or butter, melted

instructions: Blend the oats in a blender to a fine powder. You'll have about 3/4 cup oat flour.
Beat milk and egg together in a medium bowl. Stir in melted butter.
Add oat flour, salt, baking soda, and baking powder. Stir until just combined. Let batter rest 10 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat, grease lightly. Spoon in batter, about 1/4 cup per pancake.
Cook until bubbles on top break, flip, cook until golden on both sides.
recipes.notes: From My Pantry. Makes 8 pancakes.

recipes.name: Chicken Stock

ingredients.name: Meaty chicken parts or whole chicken

instructions: Put chicken in a large pot and add 1.5 gallons cold water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then lower so broth is barely simmering.
Skim foam that rises to the top but leave some fat.
After skimming, add vegetables, salt, peppercorns, and herbs. Simmer 3 to 4 hours.
Turn off heat, let cool a bit, strain, and discard solids.
Ladle stock through a fine-mesh sieve into containers.
recipes.notes: From My Pantry. Makes about 5 quarts.

recipes.name: Hummus with Preserved Lemon
instructions: Drain and rinse chickpeas. Place in a pot with onion, carrot, all but one garlic clove, salt, dried chile, and water to cover by an inch.
Bring to a boil and simmer until tender, 1 to 2 hours. Cool in cooking liquid. Discard onion, carrot, chile.
Reserve some cooking liquid and drain chickpeas.
Pound remaining garlic clove and salt to smooth paste. Add preserved lemon and pound until combined.
Add chickpeas and mash. Add tahini, olive oil, lemon juice, cumin, and cayenne. Mix to smooth, adding reserved liquid as needed.
Adjust salt. Garnish with olive oil and cumin or cayenne.
recipes.notes: From My Pantry. Makes about 2 cups.

recipes.name: Homemade Yogurt
instructions: Warm milk in a heavy-bottomed nonreactive pot over low heat, stirring often, until 185°F.
Remove from heat and cool to 112°F, whisking to speed cooling.
Locate a warm spot (around 110°F).
Sprinkle starter over milk, let sit 2 minutes, stir gently to dissolve.
Cover pot with a lid and wrap in a thick towel. Place in warm spot for 6 to 12 hours until thick. Longer = tangier.
Refrigerate.
recipes.notes: From My Pantry. Makes 6 to 8 cups.

recipes.name: Whole-Wheat Flatbreads
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, salt, and baking powder.
Stir in water and oil. Knead briefly to form a soft, moist dough.
Cover with kitchen towel and rest 30 minutes.
Divide dough into 16 balls. Roll each ball into a 6-by-3-inch oval.
Heat cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Cook two flatbreads at a time until browning, about 2 minutes per side.
Wrap in a clean kitchen towel while warm.
Before serving, hold each flatbread briefly over an open flame, turning until lightly charred.
recipes.notes: From My Pantry. Makes 16 flatbreads.

recipes.name: Candied Citrus Peel
instructions: Wash citrus and cut in half. Juice fruit and reserve for another use.
Put peels in a saucepan, cover with cold water, bring to boil, simmer 10 minutes.
Drain, cover again with cold water, boil and simmer 10 minutes more. Repeat if not tender.
Scrape out most of the white pith with a spoon. Slice peel into long 1/4-inch strips.
Return to saucepan with 4 cups sugar. Add 2 cups water and heat over low heat, stirring to dissolve sugar.
Cook slowly until peel is translucent. Turn up heat and cook syrup to thread stage (230° to 234°F).
Turn off heat and let peel sit in syrup 30 minutes. Scoop strips onto wire rack to dry overnight.
Toss strips with remaining sugar.
recipes.notes: From My Pantry. Makes about 4 cups.

recipes.name: Tisane

ingredients.name: Fresh herbs (lemon verbena, mint, lemon thyme, hyssop, chamomile, ginger)

instructions: Rinse several branches of fresh herbs.
Put them in a teapot or saucepan.
Pour boiling water over them.
Let steep for several minutes and serve.
recipes.notes: From The Art of Simple Food.

recipes.name: Fried Rosemary
instructions: Heat a small pan over medium-high heat with about 1/2 inch olive oil.
When oil is hot, add the leaves.
Fry for 1 minute, then scoop out with a slotted spoon.
Drain on absorbent paper. Sprinkle with salt and a pinch of cayenne if desired.
recipes.notes: From The Art of Simple Food II.

recipes.name: Bay Leaf Panna Cotta
instructions: Brush eight 4-ounce ramekins lightly with oil. Chill until ready.
Sprinkle gelatin over 3 tablespoons water in a small bowl. Set aside.
Combine cream, milk, sugar, lemon zest, and bay leaves in a heavy saucepan. Scrape vanilla seeds in, add bean.
Heat just to a simmer; do not boil. Remove from heat.
Pour 1 cup of hot cream over gelatin and stir to dissolve. Pour back into cream mixture and cool until just warm (110°F).
Remove vanilla bean. Strain and pour into ramekins. Cover and chill at least 6 hours.
To serve: run a small knife around inside of each ramekin, turn over onto a plate.
Serve with fresh berries or fruit compote.
recipes.notes: Adapted from The Art of Simple Food.

recipes.name: Salsa Verde (Alice Waters)

ingredients.name: Capers, rinsed, drained, and coarsely chopped

instructions: Combine all ingredients in a small bowl. Mix well and taste for salt.
Let sauce sit a while to develop flavors.
Optional: add diced shallot macerated in vinegar or 1 small garlic clove chopped fine.
recipes.notes: Adapted from The Art of Simple Food.

recipes.name: Mesclun Salad
instructions: When ready to serve, put lettuce in a wide salad bowl.
Pour half of the vinaigrette over the leaves and toss gently.
Taste. Add more dressing if needed, plus salt and pepper.
Eat immediately.
recipes.notes: Adapted from Fanny in France.

recipes.name: Galette Dough
instructions: Combine flour, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Cut 4 tablespoons of butter into the flour until mixture resembles coarse cornmeal.
Cut in remaining 8 tablespoons butter just until biggest pieces are size of large peas.
Dribble in ice water in stages until dough just holds together.
Divide dough in half, press into balls, wrap in plastic, flatten into disks.
Refrigerate at least 30 minutes before rolling.
On a lightly floured surface, roll into a 14-inch circle about 1/8 inch thick.
Transfer to parchment-lined baking sheet and refrigerate at least 30 minutes before using.
recipes.notes: From Chez Panisse Fruit.

recipes.name: Apple and Frangipane Galette
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Place galette dough on parchment-lined baking sheet. Spread frangipane in thin layer, leaving 1-inch border.
Slice apples 1/4-inch thick. Arrange in concentric circles to the center.
Fold the overhanging dough over the apples, crimping at intervals.
Brush melted butter over apple slices and onto dough border. Sprinkle sugar over pastry and apples.
Bake in center of oven. Rotate after 15 to 20 minutes. Bake about 45 minutes total.
Cool at least 15 minutes.
Make glaze: simmer reserved apple peels/cores with 1/2 cup sugar in water 25 minutes. Strain and brush over tart.
recipes.notes: Adapted from Chez Panisse Fruit.

recipes.name: Frangipane
instructions: Blend together the almond paste and sugar.
Beat in the butter.
Mix in the flour, egg, kirsch, and salt and beat until fluffy.
recipes.notes: From Chez Panisse Fruit. Makes 1/2 cup.

recipes.name: Fresh Pasta
instructions: Sift flour onto a wooden cutting board.
Make a well in flour and crack in eggs and yolks. Mix with a fork.
